Activity.description: One thing a working loop is doing: an open operation, a retry, or the pace.

oneOf.description: A tool call executing.
A turn's request in flight.
A triage's request in flight.
A compaction waiting or writing.

A failed request being tried again: `attempt` is the one that failed, of
`budget` when the loop counts them, the next at `next_at`.
The operator's pace delay between steps, ending at `until`.

Approval.description:
The decision returned by
[`Frontend::approve`](crate::frontend::Frontend::approve) (docs/README.md). A typed
line is a *redirect* — the call is rejected and the human's text is fed to the model
as the next user turn, steering it without ending the turn. Every un-run
`tool_use` still gets a paired `is_error` `tool_result` so the wire never
orphans a call (the API rejects that); the loop owns that pairing.

Serialized into the log as a gate decision's record (`Telemetry::GateDecision`,
docs/log-and-projection.md), so a rename here changes what new entries say.

oneOf.description: Run the call.
Don't run it; bail the turn.

Don't run it; reject the call and send this text to the model as the next
user message, then keep going. The human's words land as a real user turn
(after the rejection `tool_result`), so the model reads it as direction,
not tool output.

**Amend policy**, then run this call iff the amended policy now clears it
(docs/permissions.md). The orchestrator's reply at a gate: extend
the config with a [`ConfigChange`], written to the session's config file and logged as a
`Payload::ConfigEdit`. The current call does not "ride along" — the loop re-classifies it
against the new policy and only runs it if it clears, so the mechanism (not the
human's gesture) authorizes the run. `note` is the rationale, for the audit corpus.

ArchiveOutcome.description: What became of a session that was archived.

oneOf.description: Stopped, with its directory and log intact: resumable.

Removed, because it never had a turn (or its creation was cancelled while it
started): its id is free again.

ArchivedSession.description:
One archived session as `GET /sessions?state=archived` lists it: the
inventory's row, with `state` saying which collection it is from.

archived_by.description:
Who archived the session, from the `source` of the `Archived` entry that is the
last lifecycle entry; absent when it records none or the last lifecycle entry is
not `Archived` (docs/log-and-projection.md).

created_at.description: `at` of the first entry after the header, epoch milliseconds.

cwd.description: The working root whose `.efference` holds the directory.

interrupted.description:
Set when the last lifecycle entry (`Resumed` or `Archived`) is not `Archived`:
the session was open when its host went away, rather than archived on purpose.
A log with neither entry is a session that was never resumed or archived, so
it counts as open too (docs/resumption.md).

last_active_at.description: `at` of the last complete entry, epoch milliseconds.

problem.description:
Why this directory is not a readable session, when it is not. A row with
a problem keeps whatever the scan did learn.

resume_failure.description:
Why this host's last attempt to resume the session failed, until one
succeeds (the host's preparation). Unlike the row's `problem`, the session is still
resumable: this is what the last try met, not what the directory is.

title.description:
The text of the last `Title` entry, when the log has one
(docs/session-title.md).

Arrival.description:
One file that arrived in the store: where it is, and what it looks like.

Also the content of a [`ContentBlock::Attachment`](super::ContentBlock::Attachment), which is how
a turn carries the files its composer attached — so its serialized form is part of the log.

name.description:
The file's name inside its store directory — how a client addresses it
(`GET /attachments/:name`) and how a turn references an upload.

path.description: The path as the model will use it — how the store was addressed, plus the file name.

ArtifactKind.description: What a fence draws, named by its info string.

oneOf.description: `html-artifact`: a page the agent wrote.
`mermaid`: a Mermaid diagram, which the host draws in a page of its own.

ArtifactLink.description: One artifact's address, as the client entry view carries it (docs/control-api.md).

external_url.description:
The same document on the artifact-only loopback listener, for a local browser;
absent for a session outside a host.

url.description: Root-relative: a web client loads it from the origin it already uses.

AskView.description:
The `ask` topic: the question an `ask` has put to the operator
(docs/process-monitor.md), as `GET /state` and a status body say it. `null` when none
is pending.

n.description:
This question's place among the asks of one completion, which are put one at a
time.

recalled.description:
The turns withdrawn from the queue when this ask started, in the shape a recall
returns, for the submitting client to put back in its composer.

AssistantOutput.description:
The ordered assistant-output vocabulary of the session's wire dialect.

The dialect is outside the item vector so one turn cannot mix replay credentials
from different providers. Presentation and execution consume semantic accessors;
request projection consumes the concrete arm (docs/log-and-projection.md).

oneOf.description:
The content blocks of one Anthropic-Messages assistant message, in provider
order. OpenRouter's Anthropic-compatible endpoint uses the same shape.
The top-level `output` items of one OpenAI Responses result, in provider order.
One Chat Completions assistant message, as the stream assembled it.

AttachmentKind.description:
What an arrived file turned out to be — the triage signals the notification carries.

The set is deliberately small and prototype-first: enough for the model to decide whether the
file is worth pulling *without* re-deriving its content from the notice. Tunable — the right
fields are an empirical question about real pastes, not a settled schema.

oneOf.description: Valid UTF-8: byte size, line count, a sniffed shape, and the first non-blank line.
A decodable image: format, pixel dimensions, byte size.
Neither — the notice says only what it honestly knows.

AttachmentShape.description:
A coarse guess at a text attachment's shape, from its first lines. Coarse on purpose: it
steers a first move (grep vs read vs ignore) and is never relied on.

AttentionReport.description: One client's report, as `POST /attention` receives it.

active.description:
Whether the person is attending: the page is visible, focused, and has
seen recent input.

client.description: A per-page-load (web) or per-process (TUI) id the client generated.

session.description:
The session the client has open, or `None` (null or absent) on a page
that shows none (the session list).

AttentiveClient.description: A client that was attending when the moment fired.

session.description: The session it had open, if any.

Audience.description:
Which projection a [`Summary`] applies to (docs/summary.md). A `Triage` summary
replaces the range for a triage model on its own client; the main projection
ignores it, so the main model's wire bytes do not depend on it.

Axes.description:
One assessment's answers, as the model reported them: P(true) per axis, and the
sketch distribution. The two optional axes are asked only when the state
carries the thing they are about — a watch-for list, a promotion probe — so
`None` means "not asked", never "answered zero".

Recorded alongside the stance on `Spot::axes`. Entries written before the
sketch fold carry `reversible` and `sanctioned`, which are ignored on read, and
lack `sketch` and `precedent`, which default to `None`.

path_denied.description:
Names a path under a grant marked `denied` — the carve-out case, which
is a different question from being outside every grant.

path_outside.description:
Names a path outside every grant. Split from [`Self::path_denied`]
because one question asking both was four hops — resolve the move's
paths, resolve the grants, check containment, check the denies — and
scored 0.21–0.56 on plainly in-scope read-only commands.

precedent.description: What the relation request found, when the fold reached the precedent step.

sketch.description: P(level) for sketch levels 0 to 4, lowest first.

Background.description: A background process the session holds.

background.description:
Whether the call asked to be backgrounded, in which case `duration_ms`
measures the spawn and `result_bytes` the handle message — not the
command.

exit_status.description:
The status the result reported — `"1"`, or `"signal"` for a command a
signal killed. `None` means the result reported none, which for a
completed foreground command is exit zero.

handle.description:
The `p#<n>` handle of the process this call spawned (docs/process-monitor.md),
as the process monitor minted it. Present for every bash command that reached
a spawn — foreground included, since foreground and background share one
namespace — so the handle↔call join is readable off the telemetry row
without parsing result prose. `None` for a call that never spawned (a
refused command, a failed background spawn) and for logs written before
the field existed.

Block.description: What a blocked loop waits on.

oneOf.description: The operator's pace is held.
The config file does not parse and could not be restored.

parse_error.description: Why it did not parse; a read of the status prints it.

oneOf.description: A triage could not reach its model; the results are held (docs/triage.md).
A triage never produced a usable verdict; the results are held (docs/triage.md).
The config file does not parse and could not be restored (docs/permissions.md).
The operator's pace dial is held (docs/control-channel.md).

BoundAction.description:
The leaf action an allowing `agents__decide` call authorizes (docs/permissions.md).

`agents__decide` carries only a target and a handle, so the parent's ladder would
otherwise judge the decision rather than the move it authorizes. Before
classification the host binds the target's held call to the decision: the
leaf tool, its input as the child wrote it, its intent and cwd, and the chain
of sessions from the directly-targeted child down to the session holding the
leaf. The parent's fast-path, spotter, and human gate all read this instead
of the handle.

chain.description:
The session ids from that target down to the session holding the leaf,
inclusive. One entry for a direct decision; longer when the held call is
itself an allowing decision. Only participating deciders appear.

cwd.description:
The leaf session's working directory — what its relative paths resolve
against.

input.description:
The leaf call's input, as the child wrote it (its `intent` still inside,
docs/tools.md).

intent.description: The leaf call's one-line intent, lifted for the gate view.

project.description:
The leaf session's project directory, which its grants resolve against;
with `cwd`, the directories `policy::classify` runs with.

session.description: The session the parent's call directly names — the top of `chain`.

CacheMissReason.description:
Which divergence the provider named (docs/transport.md). The first four are
divergences and identify the *first* one only — the provider reports the earliest,
so a later one may hide behind it. The last two mean no comparison was produced at
all, and are not evidence that the prefix moved.

oneOf.description: A different model served the request; the cache is per model.
The system prompt differs — typically a per-request value interpolated into it.

The tools array differs: added, removed, reordered, or serialized
non-deterministically. The divergence that has cost this harness a cache before
(docs/log-and-projection.md).

Model, system, and tools all match, but an earlier entry in `messages` was
altered, reordered, or removed rather than appended to.

No fingerprint was stored for the id we named — the previous request did not
carry the object, or it aged out of the provider's retention.

No comparison was produced: a prompt-affecting parameter outside model/system/
tools/messages differs (docs/transport.md), or the divergence sits beyond the
provider's comparison horizon.

A reason this build does not know. Kept so a new provider value reads as an
unnamed miss rather than failing the whole response.

CallId.description: An Anthropic tool-use id (`toolu_…`) and its matching `tool_result` id.

CatalogList.description: The connections of the model catalog, from `GET /inference/catalog`.

CatalogModel.description:
One row as a client receives it: the stored row, the connection it belongs
to, and the rank of the matching recent pick, folded in at read time.

kind.description: Absent on the wire for a text model, the common case.

line.description:
The model line the provider files it under (Anthropic `line`: `haiku`,
`sonnet`, …), read rather than inferred from the id.

model.description: The provider-native id a session draft carries.

recent.description:
1 for the most recently and heavily picked model in the requested
project scope, counted across connections.

oneOf.description: A copy younger than the TTL.
A copy past the TTL; a refresh is under way or pending.
No copy yet; a refresh is under way or pending.
The last refresh failed and the copy is past the TTL or absent.

The connection has no usable credential (or is disabled), so no read
was attempted.

Closing.description: A turn's closing message, cut at [`CLOSING_CAP`].

bytes.description: The whole message's size and line count, so a cut can say how much it left out.

seq.description: The entry it was read from.

Cold.description:
The `cold` topic: the session's prompt cache is believed to have expired
(docs/control-api.md). The topic is `null` while the cache is believed warm, before
the first turn, on a model with no cache, and when there is nothing to compact.

context_tokens.description:
The last turn's prompt, in tokens: what reading the context cold would cost.
`null` before a turn's usage is known.

since.description:
When the cache is believed to have expired: the last request on the main prefix
plus the provider's cache lifetime.

ColdEvent.description: One step of the cold check.

oneOf.description: The loop stopped before a request on the main prefix.

context_tokens.description: What the read would cost uncached, when a turn has reported it.

since.description: From when the cache is believed expired.

oneOf.description: A person acted while the session was believed cold.
The loop left the cold check.

ColdReason.description: Why the loop stopped at its cold check.

oneOf.description: The cache is believed expired: continuing pays the context uncached.
Run without review.
Send to review, as `gate` does.
Send to review: the spotter, then the operator.

Skip the spotter and go to the operator, who can still allow it; an autonomous
session declines it.

CompactionFailure.description:
The `compaction_failure` topic: the last compaction ended without a summary
(docs/summary.md). It stands until a turn's request goes out or another compaction is
asked for, and is folded from the log, so it survives a restart.

at.description: When it failed, absolute Unix millis.

Compared.description:
One candidate's reading: the earlier call, by id, and the mean of its two
askings for `same` and for `wider`.

CompletionsMessage.description: One assistant message. Serializes as the bare object it replays as.

Condition.description: The condition, and what each one carries for its reader.

oneOf.description: Being prepared: the `starting` topic's stage and authorization.

authorizing.description: The MCP server whose authorization preparation waits on.

oneOf.description: Preparation ended without a session.
Executing a turn: what is open now, possibly nothing.
Holding a call for a decision.
Waiting on the answer to a question, `n` of `of`.

returned.description:
The queued messages the question returned undelivered (docs/process-monitor.md),
so each sender can be told its own.

oneOf.description: Its turn is done; what it said last.

The last trajectory gave up. `held_triage` is a triage holding the batch's results,
which the operator's continue retries rather than a message.
Stopped at its cold check.
Stopped until someone outside the session's drivers acts.
The runtime returned cleanly.
The runtime returned with an error.

ConfigChange.description:
What a [`ConfigEdit`] changes — the `{ which slot, new value }` reshape
(docs/permissions.md). Each variant addresses one section of the config table;
[`crate::config::policy::apply_config_change`] sets the named key (replace-at-key, last-write-wins).
Most variants set membership or a perm; [`ConfigChange::Scope`] replaces a scalar — the
narrowing edit append-only KDL couldn't do. The `watch-for` slot is unbuilt (its replace
semantics over a list are an unsettled question; add it when an initiator needs it).

**Session-visibility** (which edits notify the session) is decided by variant in
[`crate::daemon`]: `Scope` and `Path` are the perimeter the session should learn moved;
`Command` and `Tool` reach the model only through the classifier.

oneOf.description:
Clear a bash command-prefix: add `command` to the `[commands]` set. The string is the
key itself (a re-lexable command prefix); empty-args = blanket-trust the program.

Set a filesystem subtree's perms: `path` and everything beneath it (`write` implies
`read`, as in the config). **Session-visible** — moving the spatial perimeter notifies.

Grant a structured tool: set `granted` on its `[tools]` entry. `name` is the tool's
wire name, or a whole namespace as `<namespace>__*` ([`crate::record::names::tools::namespace_glob`]).

Replace the session **scope** (the perimeter prose). **Session-visible** — the boot
preamble stays frozen (re-rendering it would mutate behind the cache breakpoint), so a
live scope edit reaches the session as a notification, not a preamble rewrite
(docs/permissions.md).

ConfigEdit.description:
One config edit: a single, durable change to the policy table (docs/permissions.md).
The change vocabulary lives here, in the log types, deliberately — like [`Stance`] and
[`Origin`], the log owns its own serialized types so the wire format isn't hostage to a
config struct's layout. [`crate::config::policy::apply_config_change`] applies each [`ConfigChange`] to
the config it folds into.

change.description:
What changed: which slot, and its new value. Replace-at-key — the fold sets the addressed
key, last-write-wins, so replaying a log in order materializes the table deterministically.

note.description:
The orchestrator's one-line rationale, addressed to the session (and the corpus byproduct:
the labeled `(change, why)` pair for any future triaged approval model).

resolves.description:
Which pending proposal this entry resolves, by the `Proposed` entry's `seq` — the foreign
key from a `Committed`/`Cancelled` decision back to its proposal (the audit link, and how
the daemon drops the right entry from its pending-proposals queue). `None` for a *direct*
commit that had no prior proposal (the synchronous human gate, fs-watch) and for a
`Proposed` entry itself (a proposal resolves nothing).

state.description:
Where this edit sits in the propose→commit/cancel lifecycle
(docs/permissions.md). The fold gates on it: only [`EditState::Committed`]
takes effect (and, for session-visible keys, notifies); a [`EditState::Proposed`] entry is
inert in the effective config — it sits in the daemon's pending-proposals queue awaiting an
orchestrator's commit. The synchronous human-gate path appends `Committed` directly.

ConfigRepair.description:
The config file on disk does not parse **and** could not be restored to the
last content that did (`config::Refreshed::RevertFailed`) — the one state the
adopted-or-rejected invariant cannot reach (docs/permissions.md).

It is terminal-until-repaired rather than a notice: the effective policy in
memory is still the last good config, but the file no longer shows it, and the
file is the perimeter's readable form. Running on indefinitely would mean a
session acting under permissions nobody can inspect. Making it terminal
introduces no blocked-with-nobody-home state, because a config write is the one
operation that is never autonomous — it gates for the orchestrator even under
`--autonomous`, so a file in this condition always has an owner.

at.description:
Unix millis at which the daemon parked, absolute like every other instant
on the control channel (docs/control-api.md).

message.description:
Leads with the condition and what clears it — the same register the
`stall` topic's `message` uses.

parse_error.description: Why the file did not parse.

path.description: The file a human has to fix.

restore_error.description: Why the restore of the last good content also failed.

ConnectionCatalog.description: One connection's entry in a catalog answer.

age.description: Seconds since the copy was fetched.

ConnectionInventory.description:
One connection a host can disclose to an inference-options client. It reports
configuration status only; it never carries an endpoint or credential source.

ContentBlock.description:
A content block authored by the model or user. `Thinking` / `RedactedThinking`
carry the extended-thinking payload (docs/transport.md): `signature` is the
opaque per-block token the API mints and requires echoed **verbatim** on replay
(it rejects a modified block); `redacted_thinking` carries opaque `data` instead
of text. Images are not blocks here — a tool result's images live on
[`RawResult`], where the bytes are stored as they go on the wire.

`Attachment` is a file the operator's composer attached to a `User` turn. It
records the file's name, path, and triage signals, never its bytes: it
projects as the same notice an ambient arrival carries, and the model pulls
the file with `read` / `read_image` if it wants it (docs/inbox.md).

ContentElision.description:
The tag on a `content` a control-channel view truncated: how many bytes the view
carries, and how many the whole result holds. `GET /log/:seq` serves the rest
(docs/control-api.md).

ContextItem.description:
A single resolved context item — an inlined file (body in full) or a listed stub (read on demand).
Both render as a name tag `<name>…</name>` (docs/context.md); the name is the file's
frontmatter `name`, else its basename.

oneOf.description:
The full body rides in the preamble inside `<name>…</name>`. `path` is kept for provenance /
the boot snapshot, not rendered (the tag name is the identity).

A one-line stub `<name>{description} Read {path} for the full file.</name>`; the body is read
on demand via `path`.

A dynamic section (docs/context.md): `body` is the stdout of `command`, run
**once at boot** with the session cwd — frozen and snapshotted exactly like a static file, so
`Date = { exec = "date" }` honestly means "the date as of session boot". Renders identically
to [`Item::Inline`]; `command` is kept for provenance, not rendered.

ContextSection.description:
One rendered section: a labeled group (`heading = Some`) or a bare entry (`heading = None`).
`description` is the operator's prose hint about how to use these files (e.g. how to read or
write a memory), rendered as a `<description>` child element inside the group wrapper.

ContextWindow.description:
The model's context window and how much of it the last turn's prompt used
(docs/transport.md).

limit.description: The window, as the provider reported it at boot; `null` when it reported none.

used.description:
The last main-loop request's prompt tokens — uncached input, cache reads and cache
writes together; `null` before the first turn.

ContinueOrigin.description:
Who sent an accepted continue ([`Telemetry::Continue`]), spelled as a turn's `source`
is: `web`, `mcp[<name>]`, `session[<id>]`; absent for the operator's own command line
or TUI (docs/control-api.md).

Cost.description: The session's billed cost, where the provider prices requests (docs/transport.md).

unpriced.description: Requests that could not be priced, which make `usd` an undercount.

CreateSession.description:
Body of `POST /sessions` (docs/control-api.md): a `SessionRequest` as a
client spells it. One type on both ends — the control client serializes it,
the host deserializes it — so a new session knob is one field here. `env` is
the session's complete base environment (docs/env.md); it is applied and
dropped, never logged or echoed, which is why the type has no Debug.

`env` is optional because an omitted one is a *different request* from an
empty one. Supplied, it is the base and nothing runs; omitted, the base is
established for the session's directory from the user-wide `env_hook`, or
from the host's own environment when none is configured (docs/env.md). An
empty map is an explicit empty environment, so `{}` and omitted are different
requests.

cwd.description:
The directory the session works in. Absolute, always sent. The session's
project is this directory, or the project whose worktree it is inside
(docs/worktrees.md).

detached.description:
Outlive the session that creates this one (docs/tools.md). Meaningful only
for a session-driven `create`: a human root has no creator to end with.

env.description:
The session's complete base environment, when the caller supplies one
(docs/env.md). `None` asks the host to establish it for `cwd`.

name.description:
The session id; a minted adjective-noun pair when absent
(docs/session-title.md). A single plain path segment, as the gate's
`plain_id` requires.

refuse_authorization.description:
Fail the mount of an MCP server that asks for authorization, naming why, instead
of starting the authorization dance on the host (docs/mcp-auth.md): for a
preparation nobody may be at the host to finish.

worktree.description:
Give the session its own git worktree and start it there
(docs/worktrees.md).

CreatedSession.description:
The answer to `POST /sessions`: the id the session was reserved under. The session is
listed as `starting` and prepares after the answer.

CurrentOperations.description:
The `current_operations` topic: the upstream requests open now, the tool calls
executing, and a compaction waiting or writing. The topic is `null` rather than empty
when nothing is open; where the loop itself waits is the `loop_phase` topic.

compaction.description: The compaction asked for, while it is still to land.

requests.description: Open requests, in the order they were sent.

tools.description: Calls dispatched and not yet resulted.

Device.description: One row: an enrolled device, the holder of one TCP credential.

label.description: Display text, cleaned on the way in ([`clean_label`]).

last_seen_at.description:
Unix seconds of the last request recorded, written at most every
[`SEEN_INTERVAL_SECS`]; `None` before the first.

DeviceDelivery.description: One subscription's answer to one push.

oneOf.description: A 2xx.
404 or 410: the subscription no longer exists and was pruned.
Any other status (`status` set) or a failure before an answer.

device.description:
A short stable hash of the endpoint, so two profiles on one vendor differ
without the log holding the endpoint's secret path.

host.description: The endpoint's host (`web.push.apple.com`), which names the browser vendor.

DeviceId.description:
An enrolled device's id: 16 bytes from the OS random source, drawn fresh for
every enrollment, so a revoked id is never issued again. Public — it is the
readable half of a token and the table's key.

DeviceJoined.description: How a device got its token.

oneOf.description:
A browser showed a short code, the operator approved it at the host
(`efference devices approve`), and the browser claimed it (`crate::platform::sign_ins`).

A browser opened a sign-in link minted at the host — the one the host prints,
`efference dev open`'s, an island's — and claimed it (`crate::platform::sign_ins`).
`efference devices add`, over the host's socket.
A browser that signed in, keeping the token in its own storage.
A program given a token by `efference devices add`.

DeviceList.description: The enrolled devices, oldest first, from `GET /auth/devices`. Never a token.

DirEntry.description:
One entry of a directory listing. `kind` follows symlinks (a link to a directory lists as
a directory) while `symlink` records that the entry itself is one, so a client can show
the indirection without a second request.

modified_at.description: Absent (`null`) for a link whose target does not resolve.

name.description: Bare in a flat listing; relative to the listed directory in a recursive one.

size.description:
Bytes on disk. Reported for directories too, where it is the directory's own size and
means nothing to a reader.

DirEntryKind.description: What a listed entry is, after following a symlink.

oneOf.description: A device, socket, fifo — or a symlink whose target does not resolve.

DirListing.description:
A directory's listing. `path` is the directory's own path relative to the root, empty at
the root itself, so a client can render a breadcrumb without reconstructing it from the
URL.

recursive.description: Whether entry names are paths (recursive) or bare names (flat).

truncated.description: A cap was hit: the set is a prefix of what is there, not the whole of it.

Disposition.description:
What the agent chose to do with one notification at a triage (docs/inbox.md).
"Leave" (bump to the next triage) is the *absence* of an entry, so it isn't a variant.

oneOf.description: Promote into canonical working context (projects at the [`Triage`] position).
Clear from the inbox (logged for audit, never reaches the wire).

DormantSession.description:
One dormant session as `GET /sessions/:session` answers it: the listing's row,
and what a client offering the model switches at resume reads
(docs/resumption.md). A field the session's files cannot answer is left out.

archived_by.description:
Who archived the session, from the `source` of the `Archived` entry that is the
last lifecycle entry; absent when it records none or the last lifecycle entry is
not `Archived` (docs/log-and-projection.md).

context_tokens.description:
The prompt tokens of the session's last main-loop request: what reading the
context uncached would cost, the number the `cold` topic reports as
`context_tokens` for a hosted session. Absent when the usage record holds no
`turn` line.

created_at.description: `at` of the first entry after the header, epoch milliseconds.

cwd.description: The working root whose `.efference` holds the directory.

interrupted.description:
Set when the last lifecycle entry (`Resumed` or `Archived`) is not `Archived`:
the session was open when its host went away, rather than archived on purpose.
A log with neither entry is a session that was never resumed or archived, so
it counts as open too (docs/resumption.md).

last_active_at.description: `at` of the last complete entry, epoch milliseconds.

problem.description:
Why this directory is not a readable session, when it is not. A row with
a problem keeps whatever the scan did learn.

resume_failure.description:
Why this host's last attempt to resume the session failed, until one
succeeds (the host's preparation). Unlike the row's `problem`, the session is still
resumable: this is what the last try met, not what the directory is.

selections.description:
The main, spotter and triage selections the session last ran on, in the
shapes an `active` patch takes, read as a resume reads them
([`crate::boot::recorded_selections`]). Absent when the log cannot be read or
records none.

title.description:
The text of the last `Title` entry, when the log has one
(docs/session-title.md).

EditState.description:
Where a [`ConfigEdit`] sits in the propose→commit/cancel lifecycle
(docs/permissions.md). Append-only means the three states are **distinct
entries sharing the proposal's `seq`**, not a mutated record: an async initiator (the session's
`propose_scope`, the spotter's prefix-promotion) appends a `Proposed`, and the orchestrator later
appends a `Committed` or `Cancelled`. The synchronous human-gate path and fs-watch append
`Committed` directly (the human's gesture / file edit *is* the commit). The fold applies only
`Committed`; `Proposed` and `Cancelled` are audit-only and never reach the effective config.

oneOf.description:
Filed by an async initiator, awaiting an orchestrator decision. Inert in the effective
config; lives in the daemon's pending-proposals queue, addressed by its `seq`.
In effect: the fold applies its `change` (and, for `scope`/`paths`, notifies the session).

The orchestrator declined a `Proposed` edit. Audit-only — drops the proposal from the queue,
never touches the effective config.

EditTelemetry.description:
Fields read off an edit-shaped call's own arguments (docs/tools.md). Every
value here comes from the `input` the model wrote, so it is available for any
tool that spells its arguments this way and costs nothing to collect; nothing
is plumbed out of the editing crates.

anchor_bytes.description:
Byte length of the anchor the call matched on — the number the
anchor-discipline question is asked about.

content_bytes.description: Byte length of the replacement content.

operation.description: The call's `operation` argument, where it has one.

Effective-EffectiveTriage.description:
One effective field: the value that would be used, and where it came from.
`source: null` marks a field whose resolution *failed* — the paired issue says
why. A `value: null` with a source present is an ordinary omission.

Effective-ModelSelection.description:
One effective field: the value that would be used, and where it came from.
`source: null` marks a field whose resolution *failed* — the paired issue says
why. A `value: null` with a source present is an ordinary omission.

Effective-string.description:
One effective field: the value that would be used, and where it came from.
`source: null` marks a field whose resolution *failed* — the paired issue says
why. A `value: null` with a source present is an ordinary omission.

Effective-uint8.description:
One effective field: the value that would be used, and where it came from.
`source: null` marks a field whose resolution *failed* — the paired issue says
why. A `value: null` with a source present is an ordinary omission.

EffectiveTriage.description:
The effective triage client, flattened so it reads like the other role
selections rather than echoing the request's tagged spelling.

oneOf.description: The triage runs on the main client.
A selected connection plus the provider-native model ID sent upstream.

Enrolled.description:
A device just enrolled, with its token: the one answer that carries the token.
No `Debug`, because the token is a credential.

ErrorBody.description: The body of a non-2xx response.

detail.description:
Machine-readable context for codes that carry corrective state — the current
pending gate on a [`ErrorCode::GateMoved`]. Omitted entirely when there is none.

message.description:
The human half — surfaced verbatim by the CLI. Free to change; clients branch on
`code`.

ErrorCode.description:
The machine-readable half of an error response. Each variant has one canonical HTTP
status ([`ErrorCode::status`]), so a handler picks the code and the status follows.

oneOf.description: Malformed body, unparseable path parameter, out-of-range value. 400.

A well-formed decision the daemon doesn't implement (an unknown approval
decision, a proposal decision that is neither commit nor cancel). Distinct from
[`BadRequest`](Self::BadRequest) because the client sent valid JSON and a client
that gets this is version-skewed, not buggy. 400.
No such addressable thing — a notification id, a proposal `seq`. 404.

The addressed approval is no longer the pending gate: it was already resolved,
or the loop moved on. **409**, with the *current* pending gate in `detail` so a
client re-renders without a second round-trip. Its own code rather than a 404,
which cannot distinguish "that gate moved" from "there is no such call".

`POST /loop/continue` was asked for at a moment that has no continue in it:
the loop is running or gated, or the wire ends where re-prompting it means
nothing (docs/control-api.md). **409** — a precondition on the current
state, like [`GateMoved`](Self::GateMoved), and a client acts by showing
the message rather than by retrying.

A turn that names the question it answers, or comes from an agent, was not
delivered (docs/control-api.md): a question is pending and the turn names none,
or the question it names is not the pending one. **409**, with the pending `ask`
in `detail` (`null` when none is), so the sender can reply to the question that is
actually open. A stale reply is refused rather than delivered as a new turn.

`POST /loop/compact` at a moment with no compaction in it: the cache is not believed
expired, a gate or question is pending, a request is in flight, or everything
since the last compaction fits in the verbatim tail (backlog: cold-session.md). 409.

The addressed thing exists, but not in the state this request describes:
`PATCH /sessions/:id {"state": "active"}` naming a session this host is
already running under a different working root (docs/control-api.md). 409.
A `404` would tell the client the session is gone and a `400` that it sent
something malformed; this one tells it to read where the session actually
is. A session already running under the root the request *names* is not this
— that is the state it asked for, and it answers 200.

The session is still being prepared (docs/control-api.md): its env hook and MCP
mounts are running, so only `/state`, `/events`, and a turn are served. 409. A
client acts by waiting for the `starting` topic to clear, not by retrying now.

The daemon failed at something it was supposed to be able to do (a log append,
a config write, absent shared state). 500.

The TCP bind's auth gate (docs/web-bind.md): no valid device token on a route
that needs one. A client acts on this by re-authenticating. 401.

The TCP bind's hardening gate (docs/web-bind.md): a Host or Origin outside the
allowlist. Not a credential problem — re-authenticating won't help. 403.

`/files` was asked for something it does not serve as text — today, a file
that is not valid UTF-8 (docs/web-bind.md). A client acts by saying so
instead of rendering: no retry helps, and no other body is coming. 415.

`/files` was asked for a file past the view limit
([`files::MAX_BYTES`]). Distinct from
[`UnsupportedContent`](Self::UnsupportedContent) because the file *is* text
and a client says something different about it. 413.

Escalated.description:
One escalation of a held call: who passed it up, to whom, and the note it carries
for whoever decides next (docs/permissions.md). The gate topic and the status view
both carry these (docs/control-api.md).

source.description:
Who escalated, spelled as a turn's `source` is: `session[<id>]`, `mcp[<name>]`;
`null` for the operator's own command line.

to.description: The session it went to; `null` for the operator.

Escalation.description: One accepted escalation of a held call ([`Telemetry::Escalation`]).

note.description: The escalator's note to whoever decides next.

source.description:
Who escalated, spelled as a turn's `source` is: `mcp[<name>]`, `session[<id>]`.
Absent for the operator's own command line.

to.description: The session the call is routed to now; absent when it went to the operator.

Exclusion.description:
Why an assistant entry is **record-only**: it stays in the log for audit, projection
skips it, and the loop asks again (docs/transport.md). Skipping it is what lets the
next request re-send the same bytes and ride the cached prefix.

oneOf.description:
The upstream produced no usable turn: the stream died before finalizing, finalized
with no content and no usage, or the request itself failed. The provider has no
record of the generation and does not stand behind it.

The model finalized a completion with neither prose nor a call: reasoning alone, or
text that is empty or whitespace. The provider stands behind it, but it ends
nothing a reader can act on, so it is not taken as the turn's end.

ExitOutcome.description:
How a process ended (docs/process-monitor.md) — the structured form of the prose
the exit notification carries.

oneOf.description: Exited normally with this status code.

Terminated by a signal, which reports no code — `kill_process`, the
teardown sweep, or a kill from outside the harness.

The OS reported no status at all (the wait itself failed). Distinct from
a signal: nothing is known, rather than something specific.

FiledNotification.description: The answer to `POST /notifications`: where the notification arrived in the log.

seq.description:
The arrival entry's seq. Absent for a notification on a slot, which has no entry
until a triage shows it.

Footer.description:
What a read of the status carries below the condition; subscription notifications
leave it out.

context_limit.description: The model's context window, in tokens.

context_used.description: The last turn's prompt, in tokens.

cost.description: The session's cost, where the provider prices requests.

held.description:
The operator holds the session: nothing queued runs until the hold is released
(docs/control-channel.md).

queued.description: Each queued turn's `source`, in submission order: `None` for the operator.

ForgottenProject.description: The answer to `DELETE /projects`: the identity that was forgotten.

Gate.description:
The `gate` topic: the call held for a decision, as `GET /state` surfaces it — the
ephemeral control state the log does not record, since it stores only the result.
`null` when no gate is open.

acting_on.description:
The leaf action this approval authorizes, when the held call is a bound
`agents__decide` (docs/permissions.md). `None` for an ordinary gate.

escalations.description:
Each time the call was passed up undecided, in order (`decide` with `escalate`,
docs/permissions.md); the last names whom it is routed to now.

grant.description:
The one grant this gate offers, decided at the rung that held the call
(docs/permissions.md). `None` when no single change is confidently the one.

reason.description:
The spotter's one-line reason for routing this call to the human, if it gated via the
spotter (docs/permissions.md) — read from the `Spot` audit entry the spotter logs *before*
the gate. Lets the client show *why* a call is held without a new side channel. `None` when
no spotter verdict preceded the gate.

decision.description:
The decision as the loop received it: approve, abort, redirect with its
message, or a config edit with its change.

note_submission.description:
The submission id of the turn that carries the decider's note, for an allow
sent with one (`decide`, docs/tools.md). The note is a user turn of its own,
delivered with the call's result; this names it, so a reader of the log can tell
it from a message the same sender wrote for another reason.

source.description:
Who decided, spelled as a turn's `source` is: `web`, `mcp[<name>]`,
`session[<id>]`. Client-asserted, like an interrupt's; absent for the
operator's own command line or TUI.

GateGrant.description:
The one grant a gate offers alongside approve and abort (docs/permissions.md): the
change a client commits unchanged as the `config_edit` decision, and the label that
names what it allows ("always allow reading /work/refs"). Surfaced on `/state`'s
`gate` topic (docs/control-api.md); never logged until committed.

HeldCall.description: A held call, as its decider reads it.

call_id.description:
The provider's id for the call, which the approval route takes; `decide` maps
the handle to it.

escalations.description:
Each time the call was passed up undecided, in order; the last names whom it is
routed to now (docs/permissions.md).

held_because.description: Why it was held, in plain words (docs/permissions.md).

summary.description: What it does: a command, or the arguments (`transcript::call_summary`).

InferenceIdentity.description:
The roles a hosted session was created with, for `GET /state`'s
`session_identity` and the boot report (docs/control-api.md). Display only:
upstream requests carry the native `model` alone.

InterruptOrigin.description:
Where an interrupt came from. Both fields are client-asserted and unverified,
like a turn's `source`; a client that says nothing leaves both absent
(docs/control-api.md).

source.description:
Who interrupted, spelled as a turn's `source` is: `web`, `mcp[<name>]`,
`session[<id>]`. Absent for the operator's own command line or TUI.

Interruption.description:
What an interrupt stopped (docs/control-channel.md): carried by
[`WireState::Interrupted`], whose line is rendered from it.

after_ms.description:
How long the call had run, in milliseconds. `None` when the interrupt came during
the triage, after the call had finished.

by.description: Who interrupted, spelled as a turn's `source` is; `None` for the operator.

killed.description: The call's process group was killed, so the command did not finish.

InventoryList.description:
The host's configured connections, from `GET /inference`, sorted by name. Whether each
can be used, and nothing that would let a client reach it: no endpoint, no credential.

IssueCode.description:
The closed issue vocabulary. A client may render an unknown code by its
`message` alone, but every code here is one it can special-case.

oneOf.description: The field is needed and absent.
The JSON value is the wrong type for the field.
A numeric field is outside its accepted range.
The value is well-formed but selects nothing that exists.
The connection is configured, but its credential is disabled or did not load.
The selected project config could not be read or parsed.

Keep.description:
What of a tool result survives on the canonical wire (docs/triage.md).
Ranges are 1-based inclusive line spans, interpreted against the first
`TRIAGE_LINE_CAP` lines — the set the triage showed the model.

oneOf.description: Keep every (shown) line.
Keep nothing — only the `note` breadcrumb survives.
Keep these line ranges (the model's `retain(lines=…)` choice).

KeepaliveSkip.description:
What the keepalive is doing other than pinging normally, published as
`usage.keepalive_skipped` (docs/control-api.md). Absent from the state while pings
go out on schedule, or when the keepalive was never armed (no prompt cache,
interval zero): it records a decision the loop made, not a configuration.

oneOf.description:
The last ping discarded output that the refresh would not repay against the
current prefix (docs/transport.md). Re-evaluated every tick: the stance ends
when the prefix grows past break-even.

completion_usd.description:
That ping's completion cost in USD, when the endpoint billed it inline or
the session's prices could compute it; `null` on the token-ratio rule.

output_tokens.description: Output tokens the last ping generated.

prefix_tokens.description: The prompt tokens the next ping would read: the main prefix as it stands.

premium_usd.description:
What a cold read of that prefix would cost beyond a warm one, in USD;
`null` on the token-ratio rule.

oneOf.description:
The upstream refused the ping request itself, which would be refused
identically next tick. The one stance that does not end: the loop stops.

The upstream answered with a limit that holds until it resets (a plan's usage
limit). Pinging resumes after the next real turn, which is the first request
that can learn the limit has passed.

resets_at.description: When the limit resets, epoch milliseconds, where the refusal says.

at.description: When the loop reached this stance, absolute Unix millis.

Landing.description:
Where a submitted turn went: the `delivery` a `POST /turns` answer carries
(docs/control-api.md), and the one the `verbs` topic says a turn would get now.

oneOf.description: It answered the question it named.
The loop takes it at once.
It waits in the queue for the loop's next juncture.

An agent's turn, queued behind the operator's pace hold until it is released
(docs/control-channel.md).

LastCacheMiss.description:
The most recent cache miss the provider attributed, as `GET /state` publishes it
(docs/control-api.md). The reason is the provider's own spelling, and two of the six
values — `previous_message_not_found` and `unavailable` — mean no comparison was
produced rather than naming a divergence, so a client that renders this as a
*cause* has to say so for those two.

`at` is absolute wall-clock millis, like `last_request_at` and for the same reason
(docs/control-api.md): an elapsed-time field changes on every read, which under
level-triggered emission means the topic never goes quiet.

cache_missed_input_tokens.description:
The provider's byte-derived estimate of the prefix that fell after the
divergence. Absent on the reasons that carry none.

created_by.description:
The session that commissioned this one, when a session did
(docs/tools.md). Absent for a human root.

cwd.description:
The session's project directory, so a client can keep to its own
project's sessions on a host that serves several
(docs/control-channel.md).

processes.description:
Live background processes the session holds (docs/process-monitor.md). Ending
it reaps them, which is why a listing carries the count.

status.description: What the session is doing, as a single word.

working.description:
The session's working directory, when it is not the project: a session in
a git worktree (docs/worktrees.md).

ListedStatus.description:
What a listed session is doing, in one word: `starting` while its environment and MCP
servers are prepared, then the loop's phase as a list surface can show it without one
state read per row.

oneOf.description: Being prepared: no loop exists yet.
A request, a batch of calls, or a timed delay.
Waiting with nothing queued.
Holding a call for a decision.
Waiting on the operator's reply to a question.
An idle loop whose last trajectory gave up, or a triage held without a verdict.
Stopped at its cold check mid-turn.
Stopped on a held pace or a config file to repair.

LocatedToolCall.description:
A tool call and the entry that carries it, from `GET /tool_calls/:call_id`. A call is
embedded in an `Assistant` entry rather than being one, so this is its address.

LogEntry.description: One immutable, ordered record in the log.

source.description:
Who submitted this entry, when that is not the operator
(docs/control-api.md): the client's self-chosen label — `web`,
`mcp[<name>]`, or `session[<id>]`. `None` on operator turns and on every
entry the loop originates itself. Unlike `submission_id`, this **is**
projected: a `User` entry with a source opens its wire block with a
`source:` line (docs/log-and-projection.md). Skipped when `None`, so
unsourced entries and pre-existing logs read back and serialize
unchanged.

submission_id.description:
The submission id of the `POST /v1/turns` this entry realized
(docs/control-api.md): client-minted when the body carried one,
daemon-minted otherwise, `None` on entries the loop originates itself
(redirects, handoff notes). **Log metadata only** — never projected,
like `at` and `turn` (docs/log-and-projection.md). Clients key delivery
reconciliation on it; it also records which socket submission produced
the entry, for audit.

LoggedInference.description:
The inference identity persisted in a boot [`Payload::Preamble`].

This is deliberately a log-owned shape rather than the control/configuration
selection type. Boot copies the three facts offline readers need into this
record, so a rename in the live configuration model does not change how an
existing log deserializes (docs/log-and-projection.md).

LoopPhase.description:
Where the loop is now. Exclusive: what is in flight beside it — open requests,
running tools, a compaction — is the `current_operations` topic.

oneOf.description: Waiting for a turn, a continue, or an inbox wake.
A model request is in flight: a turn's, or a triage's (the idle triage included).
Tool calls are running, the spotter's judgement inside a batch included.

A wait that ends on a timer: a finite pace delay, or the pause between upstream
attempts. `until` is absolute Unix millis.

Waiting on a decision from outside the loop at an approval gate. An autonomous
decline is decided inside the loop and never enters it.
Waiting on the operator's answer to an `ask`.
Stopped at the cold check, waiting for a person before an uncached read.

Stopped until someone outside acts, for a reason that is not a gate, an ask,
or a cold park.

LoopResource.description:
The loop resource (`GET /loop`, `PATCH /loop`, docs/control-api.md): the operator's
dials and where the loop is, each the value — and the name — of its state topic.

oneOf.description:
The session's agent, in a `consolidate` call, with the region in view
(docs/consolidate.md).
The harness, through a model that read the digest (docs/summary.md).

MessagesOutputBlock.description: One ordered content block in an Anthropic-Messages assistant message.

oneOf.description: Visible thinking plus the opaque signature required for replay.
Safety-redacted thinking whose only replay representation is opaque data.

ModelKind.description:
What a listed model does (docs/model-catalog.md): produce a turn, or answer
typed questions about a state without producing one (a decision model, which
only the spotter can use — docs/permissions.md).

A row inherits its kind from where it was listed: a connection whose provider
serves no turns lists only decision models, and OpenRouter declares it per
entry in `architecture.output_modalities`.

ModelRole.description:
The role a model is being chosen for. The one place the rule for which models
a role may be offered lives, so the host's `?role=` filter and the TUI's
pickers cannot differ on it (docs/model-catalog.md).

ModelSelection.description: A selected connection plus the provider-native model ID sent upstream.

oneOf.description: An approval gate opened.
An `ask` was posed.
A turn ended and the loop went idle.

NewerVersion.description:
The `newer_version` topic: the newest release the host's update check found, while it
is newer than the host (docs/update-check.md), and the command that installs it. Host
state, the same on every session of a host.

url.description: Where the release's files are published.

version.description: The version as the release names it: `0.2.0`.

Notification.description:
An out-of-band notification (docs/inbox.md): freeform `body` + `source`, optionally
bound to a logical `slot` (a later notification on it supersedes this one while queued).
Immutable; once logged as a [`Payload::Ambient`] its arrival `seq` is its id.

wake.description:
Must-wake (docs/inbox.md): the loop pins this at its first show whatever the
triage decides. Recorded on the arrival entry so a restart keeps it.

OpenCompaction.description: A compaction still to land (docs/summary.md), published as its `state`.

oneOf.description: Accepted; its summarizing request not yet sent.

cut.description: The last seq the summary covers.

since.description: When this state began, absolute Unix millis.

warm.description: Asked of a session whose cache was believed live.

oneOf.description: Its summarizing request has been sent.

OpenRequest.description: A request that has been sent and not closed.

oneOf.description: Handed to the transport; no stream event yet.

An attempt was refused and the transport is trying again: `attempt` is the one
that failed, `status` the refusal's.
The first stream event arrived.

request.description: The id the request's log entries share (docs/log-and-projection.md).

since.description: When this stage began, absolute Unix millis.

PaceView.description:
The `pace` topic: the operator's between-turns dial (docs/control-channel.md) — loud to
the operator's clients, never logged or projected.

held.description: The hold: the loop waits at its next juncture until the operator releases it.

speed_ms.description: The delay between steps, in milliseconds.

Park.description: Why a loop is parked at its cold check.

oneOf.description: The cache is believed expired; continuing reads `context_tokens` uncached.
A compaction summarized the history while it waited.

PatchSession.description:
A partial update to a session: the fields present are the ones being changed.

One type for every field a patch can carry, so a new one is a field here and
nothing else. `state` is the only one that describes the session; the rest
supply what the transition needs.

connection.description:
The main model: a connection and a native model id, or the `connection/model`
slug as `model` alone.

cwd.description:
The working root whose `.efference` holds this session. Absolute.

Required to make a session `active`, because a host serving several roots
cannot tell which one a dormant id belongs to; not read by an `archived`
patch, which acts on a session this host is already running.

env.description:
This attempt's base environment, when the caller supplies one
(docs/env.md). `None` asks the host to establish it for `cwd`, as a
creation's is.

reauth.description:
MCP servers to re-authorize, discarding stored credentials first. Only read
by an `active` patch, and not a property of the session: the same request
that reopens a session says what to bring up with it.

refuse_authorization.description:
Fail the mount of an MCP server that asks for authorization instead of
starting the dance on the host (docs/mcp-auth.md). Only read by an `active`
patch: a resume nobody may be at the host to finish.

source.description:
Who is asking, spelled as a turn's `source` is (`web`, `mcp[<name>]`,
`session[<id>]`); recorded on the `Archived` entry of an `archived` patch and
read by nothing else (docs/log-and-projection.md).

state.description:
What to make the session's lifecycle be. Omitted leaves it alone — a patch
that changed nothing is refused rather than read as agreement.

supervisor.description:
Set this running session's supervisor to the session named, or clear it with
`null` (docs/permissions.md). Absent leaves it alone. Not combined with
`state` in one patch.

Payload.description:
The content of a log entry. Immutable once appended; curation never mutates
a payload's `raw`, only flips a [`WireState`] (docs/README.md).

oneOf.description: Prose (and, later, richer blocks) authored by the user / operator.

One model turn in its provider dialect's ordered output vocabulary.

Both Messages content blocks and Responses output items are ordered arrays on
their native wires. Keeping that order in the record makes projection a copy of
provider-authored structure rather than a reconstruction from grouped fields
(docs/log-and-projection.md).

excluded.description:
`Some` = the entry is **record-only**, and why ([`Exclusion`]): the upstream
produced no usable turn (its `why` the provider's error verbatim when one
arrived, a harness-written note for a silent close; a stream that finalizes
empty also carries [`StreamDiagnostics`], because nothing else about it
survives anywhere), or the model finalized with neither prose nor a call.
The content (often the only copy anywhere) stays in the log for audit, but
[`project`] skips the entry entirely, so the loop's next request re-sends the
same bytes. The assistant-side analogue of a [`WireState`] verdict: the mark
lives in the entry because projection is deterministic over the log alone
(docs/log-and-projection.md). `None` (the default; skipped when serializing,
so finalized entries are byte-identical) = a finalized turn, projected as
always.

[`project`]: crate::record::project::project

oneOf.description:
The result of running one tool call. `raw` is immutable; curation only
flips `wire`.

The final wire decision for a previously captured pending result.
Raw output stays on the referenced entry (docs/triage.md).

A fact about how the session ran rather than what it said (the
[`Telemetry`] family): projects to nothing, and every reader that renders a
session skips it (docs/log-and-projection.md).

The session was reopened from its log by a later host process
(docs/log-and-projection.md). Projects the restart notice at its position: how
long the session sat, which background processes it no longer monitors, and
which calls were dropped because they started and never returned.

The session was archived on purpose (`DELETE /sessions/:id`, `PATCH {"state":
"archived"}`, or the end of its creator): the counterpart of [`Resumed`]. The later
of the two is the session's lifecycle, which a host restart reads to tell a
deliberate archive from a session interrupted by the host's loss
(docs/resumption.md). Projects to nothing, like [`Telemetry`].

`source` is who archived it, spelled as a turn's `source` is (`web`,
`mcp[<name>]`, `session[<id>]`); client-asserted and unverified, and absent when
the caller named none, as for the operator's own command line or TUI, and for the
end of a creator (docs/log-and-projection.md).

[`Telemetry`]: Payload::Telemetry

Text that replaces a range of the transcript, made by the agent's
`consolidate` call or by the harness's compaction (docs/summary.md).
Projects the text where the range ends and elides the range
(docs/log-and-projection.md).

A triage verdict (docs/triage.md) — the durable record of a throwaway
triage's decision. The fork's *transcript* stays throwaway; its *decision* is
logged here for audit / introspection / triager-quality work. Projects as
audit only, except it emits a block per **pinned** notification (its `inbox`)
at this entry's tail-ward position (docs/inbox.md).

An out-of-band notification (docs/inbox.md), logged at **arrival** — or, for one
bound to a slot, when a triage first shows it. Pure audit on the canonical
wire (it projects to nothing); a *pinned* one is emitted by its resolving
[`Triage`], at that entry's position. Its `seq` is its durable id (the handle
the `retain` inbox verdict references); whether a triage has shown it is
[`Triage::shown_through`].

A spotter verdict (docs/permissions.md) — the durable record of the
independent permission rung's decision on one gated tool call. Like
[`Triage`], the deciding round-trip is throwaway but its *verdict* is logged:
the audit answer to "why did this call get through (or stop)?" and the corpus
for any future triaged approval model. Projects to nothing — it is audit
only, never on the canonical wire. Fast-path clears are deliberately *not*
logged; the spotter is the first permission rung that earns an entry.

One lifecycle fact about a background process — its mint or its exit
(docs/process-monitor.md). The process monitor's registry is ephemeral, but a
`p#<n>` handle appears in prose (the backgrounding result, the exit
notification) that outlives it, so these entries are what a reader of a
recorded session — or a restarted daemon — resolves the handle against.
Metadata only: the command, the spawning call, the spawn time, the exit
status and duration. A process's *output* is the registry's bounded
best-effort capture and is deliberately not recorded here.

Projects to nothing, like [`Telemetry`] — the exit still reaches the
model as an [`Ambient`] notification, and this is the audit record beside
it, not a second copy on the wire (docs/log-and-projection.md).

[`Telemetry`]: Payload::Telemetry
[`Ambient`]: Payload::Ambient

A config edit — the durable record of one change to the policy table
(docs/permissions.md). The config-edit loop turns a deny into
negotiation: an orchestrator (human or coordinating session) edits the session's
config, and the change lands here. Effective policy = base config + the fold of these
(see [`effective_config`]); the log is the source of truth for what changed, exactly as
it is for everything else (docs/log-and-projection.md). The fold is **replace-at-key**
(last-write-wins, order-defined) — materializing a table from an ordered log, like a
database replaying its write-ahead log. Audit-only on the wire — it projects to nothing,
like [`Spot`]; its effect reaches the model *by key*: a `commands`/`tools` edit only
through the classifier, while a **session-visible** edit (`scope`, `paths`) *also*
surfaces as an [`Ambient`] notification (an optional tail append — never a re-render of
the cached preamble; see [`crate::daemon`]) so the session learns its perimeter moved.

[`effective_config`]: crate::config::policy::effective_config
[`Ambient`]: Payload::Ambient

The boot preamble snapshot (docs/context.md): the system prompt exactly as this
session's requests carry it, appended **once at boot** and again by a resume that
changes a role or the main model (docs/resumption.md). The preamble folds in
`[context]` file contents that drift on disk between boots, so it is not
reconstructable from `config + current files` — this entry makes the log the
complete record of the wire (docs/log-and-projection.md). Audit/replay only: it
projects to nothing (the system prompt rides the request's `system` field, never
the `messages` array); the `wire` dev view reads it back instead of re-resolving
files from disk.

The prompt is held as two strings that concatenate to the wire's `system`:
`identity`, the line naming the model ("You are gpt-6.1-sol."; empty on a log
whose prompt predates the line), and `body`, everything after it, frozen at boot.
A resume on another main model replaces `identity` and repeats `body` byte for
byte ([`Payload::preamble_system`] assembles them).

`context` carries the **structured** `[context]` listing (name / `path` / description
per item) the `body` was rendered from, snapshotted **additively** so the
listing survives as a fold over the log — the source `project` re-renders a surfaced
context item from (docs/triage.md), the same way it looks up pinned
notification bodies. `identity` and `body` stay the byte-exact wire truth; `context`
never touches the wire. `#[serde(default)]`: logs predating the field read back an
empty listing.

inference.description:
The fixed main inference identity chosen when this session booted:
connection, provider, and provider-native model id. It is log metadata
only — an offline reader uses it to derive the historical dialect and
projection placements, while `project` emits nothing for it
(docs/log-and-projection.md). `None` on pre-identity logs.

roles.description:
The spotter and triage selections, written only by a resume that changed
one; absent means the header's stand (docs/resumption.md).

oneOf.description:
The session's title — one line saying what the session is for
(docs/session-title.md). Written by the title peek after a trajectory ends,
or by an operator over the control channel; the latest entry is the current
title, which the `session_identity` topic carries. Appended even when the
triage kept the previous text, so the log records that the question was asked.
Log metadata: it projects to nothing, like [`Telemetry`], and never
touches the wire or the cached prefix (docs/log-and-projection.md).

[`Telemetry`]: Payload::Telemetry

The session's own git worktree was created at boot: path, branch, base commit, and
git's output and exit status, which carry the project's `post-checkout` hook's
result (docs/control-channel.md). Projects to nothing, like [`Telemetry`]; appended
right after the boot [`Preamble`].

[`Preamble`]: Payload::Preamble

The endpoint refused a request carrying images, and the same request with
them withheld succeeded (docs/transport.md). From here the session's requests
carry a placeholder in each image's place and the tool layer refuses new
images; a resumed session reads this entry back to restore both. `refusal`
is the provider's error. Projects to nothing, like [`Telemetry`]: the placeholder
is the client's encoding, not this entry's projection.

[`Telemetry`]: Payload::Telemetry

PendingNotification.description:
One pending ambient notification, as the `notifications` topic lists it (docs/inbox.md):
an arrived notification not yet shown by a triage, or a slot notification still queued.

seq.description:
The arrival entry's `seq`, the handle a triage's verdict addresses. Absent for a
slot notification, which has no entry until it is shown.

wake.description:
Must-wake (docs/inbox.md): the loop pins this at its first show whatever the
triage decides, so an idle agent gets a turn to act on it. Set by the
harness for a delegated child's status, never by a client.

PendingProposal.description:
One async config edit awaiting an orchestrator decision
(docs/permissions.md). Filed by a `Proposed` [`ConfigEdit`](crate::record::log::ConfigEdit) append (the
session's `propose_scope`, the spotter's prefix-promotion); the orchestrator-above commits or
cancels it, which drops it from the queue. Unlike a
[`PendingNotification`](super::PendingNotification), the proposal
**already has a durable `seq`** (the `Proposed` entry's), so that *is* its id — no
queue-local counter.

change.description:
The change being proposed; the committing entry copies it self-contained so the fold stays a
pure per-entry filter (docs/permissions.md).

seq.description:
The `seq` of the `Proposed` log entry — the proposal's id, which the orchestrator's
commit/cancel references.

PendingSignIn.description:
A pending sign-in as the approving side sees it: the label the browser gave and when
it asked. There is no code field, so no listing or approval answer can carry one —
the operator approves by typing what the browser displays, never by picking from a
list (docs/web-bind.md).

label.description: Display text, cleaned on the way in ([`clean_label`]).

PendingSignInList.description:
The sign-ins waiting for approval, oldest first, from `GET /auth/pending`. A row has
the label and the time but never the code: approval is typing what the browser shows.

Perms.description:
Read/write permission a [`Config::paths`] grant carries. `write` implies `read` at check
time (see [`crate::config::policy`]); both default `false`, so a bare `{ }` / `false` grants nothing.
Serialized as the `role` topic reports a grant (docs/control-api.md).

PlanLimit.description: The windows for one independently metered allowance.

name.description: The backend's display name, when supplied.

PlanSnapshot.description: The plan and limits as of the most recent Codex response that carried them.

limits.description: Independently metered allowances, keyed by normalized limit id.

observed_at.description: When this snapshot was read, as absolute Unix millis.

type.description: The subscription plan type, such as `plus`.

resets_at.description: Absolute Unix millis; the backend sends seconds.

used_percent.description: How much of the window is spent, from 0 through 100.

window_minutes.description: Window length, absent when the header is missing or malformed.

Precedent.description:
What the relation request read: of the `candidates` earlier calls asked about,
how many the model read as the `same` action and how many as `wider`, with the
number the move's level required.

compared.description:
Each candidate's reading, in the order asked. The counts above are these
under the fold's cut; recording the figures is what lets a different cut be
replayed, and a surprising clear be traced to the approved call it matched.

required.description: `None` when no number of precedents clears the level.

PreviewIssue.description:
Why a field could not be used as given. `field` names the request field, so a
client can attach the message to the control the operator is editing.

`field` is a `Cow` rather than a `&'static str` because the type crosses the
wire in both directions: the host builds every issue from a literal, and a
control client decodes the same type back (docs/control-api.md).

ProcessEvent.description:
One lifecycle fact about one background process, addressed by the
spawn-minted ordinal (docs/process-monitor.md).

id.description:
The spawn-minted ordinal — bare, as routes and frames carry it; rendered
`p#<n>` in prose by [`crate::tools::process_monitor::handle`].

ProcessEventKind.description:
The two halves of the record. Two variants of one payload rather than two
payloads: they share the id that joins them, and a reader folding a log for
"what was `p#3`" wants both under one match.

oneOf.description:
The process entered the background namespace — spawned with `background:
true`, or adopted by the handoff (docs/process-monitor.md).
The process ended. Written by the drain task that saw the exit.

ProcessExit.description:
How a process ended and how long it ran (docs/process-monitor.md). Also the
exit half of a [`ProcessRecord`](crate::tools::process_monitor::ProcessRecord), so the
live registry and a log fold answer with one type.

duration_ms.description: Wall-clock milliseconds from spawn to exit.

ProcessOutputRead.description: One cursor read of a process's retained output, from `GET /processes/:id/output`.

cursor.description: Pass back as `since` to resume after what this read returned.

lost.description:
Bytes between the caller's cursor and the earliest retained byte, dropped at the
retention cap and reported rather than skipped.

output.description:
The retained bytes from the caller's cursor to the end, lossily decoded. Empty when
the cursor is already at the end.

ProcessRecord.description:
One process, running or exited — the durable answer to "what was `p#<n>`"
(docs/process-monitor.md).

call_id.description: The `tool_use` id of the call that spawned this process.

exit.description:
How it ended: status, duration, and when. `None` while it runs — and also
for a process whose exit was never recorded, which is what a daemon killed
mid-run leaves behind.

id.description: The spawn-minted ordinal (rendered `p#<n>` in prose; bare here and in routes).

muted.description:
Dismissed-from-view. A property of a *live* view, so a log-derived record
reads `false` — the log records what a process was, not what a since-dead
daemon was showing.

pid.description:
The OS pid — an attribute, never the identifier (docs/process-monitor.md). For
a log-derived record it is a breadcrumb for reading contemporaneous system
logs: pids are recycled, so it addresses nothing after the fact.

running.description:
`false` once the process has exited. The field the listing's
representation has no need for (it carries only running processes) and
this one does, because it answers for both.

spawned_at.description: Absolute Unix millis, as [`ProcessState`](super::ProcessState) carries it.

ProcessSpawn.description:
What a process was, recorded at the moment its handle became a fact a reader
can encounter (docs/process-monitor.md).

at.description:
When the process **spawned** — not when this entry was appended, which
differ for an adopted foreground command.

call_id.description:
The `tool_use` id of the call that spawned it — the call↔process mapping
(docs/process-monitor.md), here in a typed field rather than recoverable only
from result prose. `None` for a process registered outside a tool call.

pid.description:
The OS pid (== the process-group id). An attribute, never the identity:
pids are recycled, so a recorded one is a breadcrumb for reading old
system logs, not something a later session can address.

ProcessState.description:
One running process as `GET /processes` and the `processes` state topic carry it —
one representation for both, so the level-triggered topic and the resource listing
cannot drift (docs/control-api.md).

No `tail` and no last-chunk stamp: both change with every output chunk, and this
topic is level-triggered, so carrying them would emit a whole-topic replacement per
chunk. That content rides the ephemeral `output` class as `process_output` deltas
instead (docs/process-monitor.md). What remains changes only on spawn, exit, mute, or the
handoff flip.

background.description:
`false` while the process is the loop's in-flight foreground tool; flipped in
place by the handoff (docs/process-monitor.md).

call_id.description:
The `tool_use` id of the transcript call this process came from — the
call↔process mapping (docs/process-monitor.md). A client holding a transcript
entry finds its process here (and its output at
`GET /processes/:id/output`); a client holding a process row finds the
entry to jump to. Stamped at the mint, so a call that was backgrounded
mid-run carries the same id it did in the foreground.

id.description: The spawn-minted ordinal (rendered `p#<n>` in prose; bare here and in routes).

muted.description:
Dismissed-from-view (still running, still notifies on exit). Carried rather
than filtered so the listing is the whole truth; clients that hide muted rows
do so themselves.

pid.description:
The OS pid — an *attribute*, never the identifier (pids are recycled; the log
is durable, docs/process-monitor.md). Carried so a client or the
agent can interact with the process directly (signals, `lsof`) when the
process monitor doesn't model what it needs. `None` if the OS didn't report one.

spawned_at.description:
Absolute Unix millis. The client subtracts from its own clock; the daemon never
re-emits merely because time passed.

ProjectEntry.description:
One remembered launch location. `cwd` and `config` are exactly what `POST /sessions`
takes back, so an entry replays a launch verbatim.

config.description:
The configuration the launch named, as it was named. `null` asks creation to probe,
which is what a launch that named none did.

config_key.description:
The identity the index stored the entry under, which `DELETE /projects` takes.
Reported rather than recomputed, because recomputing re-probes the filesystem.

label.description: The directory's own name, or its full path where it has none (a filesystem root).

ProjectList.description: The entries of `GET /projects`, most recently used first.

ProposalResolution.description: The state a proposal reached, from `PATCH /proposals/:seq`: `committed` or `cancelled`.

Provider.description: Which API family fronts a session's endpoint, spelled as its name.

PushCancel.description: Why a held push never went out.

oneOf.description: The gate was approved, redirected, or aborted.
The `ask` ended without a reply.
A client submitted a turn.
The session was archived.
An active client reported viewing the session.
A newer moment replaced it.

PushKey.description:
The key a browser subscribes to push with, from `GET /push`: the machine's VAPID public
key, which is `applicationServerKey` verbatim.

key.description: Base64url of the uncompressed P-256 point.

PushRecord.description: One step in a moment's push.

oneOf.description: No client was attending, so the push went out at once.

A client was attending, so the push waits `delay_secs` to see whether the
moment resolves or is seen first. `attentive` names who was attending.
The wait ran out with the moment still standing; the push went out.
The held push was dropped.

What the push services answered: one element per stored subscription.
Empty means no device is subscribed.

The moment went to the session `to` rather than the operator, so nothing was
pushed: `to` is the session's supervisor, or for a gate the session it was
escalated to.

moment.description: The moment's number, unique within the session.

QueuedTurn.description:
A turn submitted and not yet taken by the loop, as the `queued` topic lists it
(docs/control-api.md). The same shape names the turns a recall or a question
withdrew and a failed start handed back, so a client puts each back in its composer.
A pending turn is never logged: this is the only place it is readable.

attachments.description:
The files its composer attached; absent when there are none, so a text-only turn
reads as it always has.

submission_id.description: The id the turn was submitted under, which a recall addresses.

RawResult.description:
