The full, immutable result of a tool run. Survives in the log forever; never
overwritten by triage — that is what makes every triage reversible.

content_elided.description:
Set **only by the control-channel entry view**, and only on the window and
frame copies of an oversized result: it says the `content` beside it is a
prefix, and how much of the whole string that prefix is
(`daemon/entry_view.rs`, docs/control-api.md). The mirror of
[`ResultImage::data`], which the same views omit — a Rust client parsing a
view with this shared type reads the elision as a value rather than
inferring it from a length. The log itself always writes `content` whole
and never writes this field, so it is `None` in every in-process result and
absent from every logged line.

images.description:
Images the tool returned alongside `content` (docs/log-and-projection.md).
The realized bytes live here, in the log entry itself, so projection is a
copy of stored data — never a re-read or re-encode of anything on disk.
Encoding happens once, at tool-run time. Defaulted and skipped when empty,
so text-only results (and every existing log) serialize byte-identically
to before the field existed.

RecordedRoles.description:
The spotter and triage selections a `Preamble` records after a resume changed
them (docs/resumption.md). The header holds the roles a session was created
with; the latest `Preamble` that carries this overrides it, so a switched role
survives the next resume.

ReleasedBy.description:
The person action that released a park (or would have: it is recorded whenever a
person acts while the session is believed cold).

oneOf.description: `POST /turns` (or a driver's `message`) with no `ask` pending.
`PUT /approvals/:call_id`: the decision at an approval gate.
`POST /turns` while an `ask` was pending: the answer.
`POST /loop/continue`.

RemovedDevice.description: The answer to `DELETE /auth/devices/:id`: the device whose token is refused from now on.

RequestOrigin.description:
Which request shape spent the tokens (docs/log-and-projection.md) — the tag on each
persisted usage line, so per-shape spend is a query over `usage.jsonl` rather than a
reconstruction from the canonical log.

oneOf.description: An agent-loop completion (docs/README.md).

A triage round-trip (docs/triage.md): the one riding a completion's tool
results, retries included, or the standalone idle triage that rides none
(docs/process-monitor.md).

A title peek (docs/session-title.md) — the triage model asked, off the
cached prefix, what the session is for.
A spotter assessment (docs/permissions.md) — its own prefix, its own lineage.
A cache keepalive ping (docs/log-and-projection.md).

A triage-lineage primer (docs/transport.md): the turn's own
input replayed on the own triage's client so the result triage resumes where
the main request ended. Never main-prefix evidence: it plants a resume point on
the triage lineage, not the loop's.

A keepalive ping on the triage lineage: the stored request re-sent — the last
primer, or the last result triage's request ending at its last breakpoint
(docs/transport.md). It refreshes the triage lineage's cached prefix and is never
main-prefix evidence.

The model writing a compaction's summary (docs/summary.md): its own prompt, so
it does not touch the main prefix.
A continuation of the main envelope considering a completed working span.

A retried attempt the loop recorded and re-sent — an unfinalized stream
(all-zero usage) or one that finalized unparseable (real usage;
docs/transport.md). Persisted as its own origin so it is not read as a
real main-loop request: only its non-zero usage is priced
(`Session::spawn_cost_fetch`) and it never counts as prefix evidence
(`ColdStreak::observe`).

An origin this build does not recognize — a forward-compat catch-all so a
`usage.jsonl` line written by a newer build still parses here (and, per
serde's `#[serde(other)]` contract, round-trips as this variant's own name
rather than the original one if ever re-serialized).

RequestStage.description: One stage of one upstream request (docs/log-and-projection.md).

finish.description:
On `Ended`: the provider's own word for why the output ended (`end_turn`,
`tool_calls`, `incomplete:max_output_tokens`, …), as the dialect spelled it
(`api::Finish`). Absent on other stages, on a stream that named none, and on
entries written before the field existed.

request.description:
The request's id, unique within the session: minted by the host when the
request starts, because the provider's generation id arrives late or never.
Entries of one request share it; concurrent requests interleave by it.

RequestStageKind.description: Where a request is, in the order a request passes them.

oneOf.description: The request was handed to the transport.

An attempt got a non-success status; the transport may re-send it. `attempt`
is 1-based within the request. The request stays open until the next stage.
The stream opened and its first event arrived.
The stream finalized.

The request ended without a finalized stream: an open failure, a stream that
died or ran past its ceiling, or `interrupted` (an interrupt, or
the request's future dropped).

ResolvedContext.description:
A fully-resolved `[context]` ready to render into the preamble: sections in **document order**
(docs/context.md). Each [`Section`] is a bare entry (no heading) or a labeled group.
This is what [`crate::config::env`] builds from disk at boot and freezes into the cached prefix.

ResolvedOptions.description:
Every effective field plus the issues that would stop creation. Preview
serializes this; creation refuses a non-empty `issues` and then resolves
credentials for the same selections.

ResponsesOutputItem.description:
One ordered output item returned by OpenAI Responses.

The first integration exposes custom function tools only, so these are the output
forms it can intentionally produce. `Unsupported` retains a future or unexpected
item for audit; an assembler that constructs it marks the enclosing turn record-only
rather than projecting or dispatching it (docs/transport.md).

content.description:
Visible `reasoning_text` parts; absent for most models. Replayed when
present so the item returns as the provider emitted it.

encrypted_content.description:
Opaque continuation state. Populated by default in stateless mode
(`store: false`); complete only on `response.output_item.done`.

summary.description: Visible `summary_text` parts. May be empty even when the model reasoned.

arguments.description:
The provider's exact JSON-encoded argument string. This is the replay
authority; execution parses it on demand rather than storing a second copy.

id.description:
The output item's identity (`fc_...`), distinct from the call/result join
key. Optional on the wire.

ResponsesReasoningSummary.description: One `summary_text` part of a reasoning item.

ResponsesReasoningText.description: One `reasoning_text` part of a reasoning item.

ResultImage.description:
One image in a [`RawResult`]: the exact bytes projected onto the wire, plus
the dimensions of the image as encoded. `width`/`height` are log metadata
(audit, TUI, token math) — the wire image block carries only `media_type` +
`data`; the dimensions the *model* needs ride in the result's text content,
written by the tool.

data.description:
Standard base64 of the encoded image, stored exactly as it will appear
in the wire block's `source.data`. `#[serde(default)]` because the
control-channel views omit this field (the bytes are fetched from
`GET /log/:seq/images/:idx` instead — `daemon/entry_view.rs`,
docs/control-api.md), and a client parsing a view with this shared type
reads it back empty. The log itself always writes it.

ResumeSwitch.description:
The model selections an `active` patch may carry, in the shapes creation takes
(docs/control-api.md). A field left out keeps what the session recorded.

connection.description:
The main model: a connection and a native model id, or the `connection/model`
slug as `model` alone.

Resumed.description:
A session reopened from its log (docs/log-and-projection.md): what the loader
knows changed across the restart, and what it set aside to continue.

gap_ms.description: Milliseconds between the last entry before the restart and this one.

lost_processes.description:
Background handles (`p#<n>`) that were spawned with no recorded exit: their
output is no longer captured, and whether they still run is unknown.

pending_calls.description:
Present only when the session resumed at an unfinished batch rather than past it:
the calls of the last live completion that have not run (or whose results are
still undecided), which the operator's next action brings back. The notice
projects after the batch's results land, not at this entry's position
(docs/resumption.md). A log written before the field existed reads as empty.

resumes_after.description:
Present only when the log ended uncleanly: the seq of the last entry this session
builds on. Entries after it and before this one stay on disk but are not
restored, and projection skips them (docs/resumption.md). A log written before the
field existed reads as `None`.

tools_changed.description:
How the tools the resumed session advertises differ from the last `tools[]` the
log recorded (docs/resumption.md). Empty (and absent from the entry) when they are
the same, or when the log never recorded one.

Retention.description:
Lines kept vs. lines triage was shown, plus the count of results whose output was
withheld outright. Cumulative over some span of the log.

kept_lines.description: Lines surviving on the wire, summed over triaged results.

shown_lines.description:
Lines triage was shown, summed over the same results — the triage, so already
capped at `TRIAGE_LINE_CAP`. Lines the cap dropped before triage ever saw them
are neither shown nor kept, and are counted in [`Self::truncated_lines`].

truncated_lines.description:
Lines the triage cap dropped before triage saw them. Reported separately: they
are not a decision anyone made, so they belong in neither side of the ratio.

withheld.description:
Results whose output was withheld because the triage failed
([`WireState::TriageFailed`]).

anyOf.description:
Clean, so its directory is removed; the branch goes too when another branch
contains its tip.
Git could not remove it, for this reason.

RetiredWorktree.description: What became of the git worktree a session made for itself when it was archived.

RetrySurface.description:
Which loop is retrying. A triage retry and a turn retry have different
consequences — a withheld triage asks the agent to re-run a call whose side
effects already stand, where an exhausted turn ends the trajectory — so the
surface is part of the state rather than a detail folded into prose
(docs/transport.md).

Returned.description: A queued message a question returned undelivered: who sent it and what it said.

ReviewLevel.description:
The operator's **review level** (docs/permissions.md): who reviews a
call the deterministic fast-path didn't clear. An ordinal dial of increasing human involvement,
runtime-settable over the control channel (unlike the frozen base config). Orthogonal to pace —
any combination is meaningful (autonomous-but-slow, human-only-and-held). Pause is *not* a
position here; that's the `held` overlay.

The order is by how much a position costs a human, which a supervising agent reduces without
eliminating: a `Supervisor` gate is answered by another session, but that session's own dial
still terminates at the operator.

Spelled on the control channel by [`as_str`](Self::as_str)'s token, which is also
its serde form.

oneOf.description:
No synchronous human: a spotter `Watch`/`Gate` redirects the model to its config
(`agent::autonomous_gate_message`) instead of blocking on an absent gate.

The supervisor reviews: a call the spotter holds is routed to the session's
supervisor — by default the session that commissioned it, settable after creation
— which resolves it with `decide`, through the ordinary approval route
(docs/permissions.md). The
default for a session that has a supervisor.

The position **resolves at routing time, never at creation**: a session with no live
supervisor — a root, a cleared pointer, or a supervisor that has since ended — reviews as
[`SpotterHuman`](Self::SpotterHuman) instead ([`crate::session::Session::resolved_review_level`]).
Resolving once at creation would leave a child whose creator died effectively unreviewed.
The supervised default: fast-path → spotter → human gate.

The human takes the spotter's role **entirely** — skip the spotter (pay no tokens, log no
`Spot`); every call the fast-path didn't clear goes straight to the human, who both gates it
and grows the allowlist by committing the grant the gate offers ([`gate_grant()`]).

The supervising session the gate is routed to: the holder's supervisor, or one
further up the supervisor chain that an escalation passed it to.

RoleView.description:
The `role` topic: the **effective** policy in force — the base config with every
committed config edit folded in, so the live perimeter rather than the boot config
(docs/permissions.md). It carries the policy's contents, not counts: an orchestrator
inspecting a subordinate needs the commands, paths and scope actually in force.

commands.description:
Each `[commands]` key with the stance it carries: an entry can carve `watch`,
`gate` or `deny` out of a broader grant, so a reader that saw only the keys would
read a carve-out as a grant.

scope.description:
The scope shared with the session; it can drift from the frozen preamble through
a live scope edit.

source.description: The base config's path, or `null` for the built-in default.

tools.description:
The `[tools]` table keyed as the file spells each entry (`efference`,
`"agents.message"`), carrying only the fields the entry sets: a `granted = false`
carve-out under a granted namespace reads as one.

watch_for.description: What the spotter watches for, which is on no other wire.

RunningTool.description: A call dispatched and not yet resulted.

command.description: The shell command, for a `bash` call; absent for any other tool.

intent.description: The call's one-line intent; `null` when it gave none.

since.description: When the call started, absolute Unix millis.

SelectionLines.description:
The line arithmetic of a `Triaged` verdict against the whole `content`: how many
lines the result has, and how many the model's view kept. Present only on a
triaged result, so a raw or elided one serializes as before.

SelectionSource.description:
The precedence branch that supplied an effective value. Closed, because a
client renders each branch differently: an inherited value is editable in
place, a requested one is the edit.

oneOf.description: The request named it.

Past explicit picks, decayed (docs/transport.md): the project mode
past its mass threshold, else the system-wide aggregate.
`[defaults]` in the user's inference config.
The main connection's provider supplied its own cheap-band spotter.
A connection that can reach a decision model supplied jev as the spotter.
The selected project config's `[transport]`.
Nothing named it, so the wire omits it and the provider decides.
Nothing named a separate triage client, so the triage shares main's.

SessionArchived.description:
The answer to `DELETE /sessions/:session`, and to a `PATCH` that makes the session
`archived`, once its teardown has run.

ended_with.description: The sessions that ended with it (its non-detached descendants), when there were any.

resumed.description: `false` on a patch, which says it reopened nothing; absent on `DELETE`.

worktree.description: The fate of the session's own worktree; absent when it made none.

SessionIdentity.description:
The `session_identity` topic: what a session is, for a client that has to name it on
screen — its id and title, the model it was configured with, and the directory it runs
in (docs/control-api.md).

All but the title are fixed at boot. They are carried as a state topic rather than a
one-shot read so a client learns them from the connect snapshot along with
everything else, and so either moving later reaches clients through the
mechanism that already delivers whole-topic replacements.

cwd.description:
The session's working directory, as the daemon knows it: what the tool
layer was built with, rendered as a path string.

id.description:
The session id (docs/session-title.md): its directory name under
`.efference/`, the `--name` a client resolves, the address a peer
messages. Fixed at creation.

inference.description:
The host connection and native model behind each role, with whether
triage shares the main client. `None` only for a session built without
boot (tests).

model.description:
The native model id boot resolved — the same string the system prompt's
identity line states (docs/context.md).

successor.description:
The session this one handed its work to with `hand_off` (docs/tools.md),
once it has. An attached client follows it there.

title.description:
The current title — the last `Title` entry's text (docs/session-title.md),
`None` before the first is written. The one identity field that moves.

SessionOptionsRequest.description:
The body of `QUERY /sessions` (docs/control-api.md): where the proposed
session would run, plus the same editable selections creation accepts.

cwd.description:
The proposed session's project root. Absolute, as creation's is: it is
what a relative `config` resolves against.

SessionResumed.description: The answer to a `PATCH /sessions/:session` that makes the session `active`.

resumed.description:
Whether this call is what made the session live: `false` for a repeat of a patch
the host had already taken, so a retry reads the same answer either way.

SessionState.description:
Whether a session is running on this host.

Deliberately two states. A deliberate archive and a host that went away are
different histories, and the inventory asks to keep them apart; they are the
same thing to act on, and an operator resuming a session does not care which
it was.

oneOf.description:
Running here. Patching this on a session that is not running reopens it
under its own id.

Stopped, with its directory and log intact. Resumable, by patching
`active` again.

SessionSupervised.description: The answer to a `PATCH /sessions/:session` that sets or clears a supervisor.

supervisor.description: The pointer as it now reads: `null` once cleared.

anyOf.description: Approved, and this was the claim's first: the token the page keeps.
Live and not yet approved: the page asks again.

SignInClaim.description:
A claim's answer from `POST /pair/claim`: the device token once the host approved, or
word that it has not yet. A claim that names nothing (used, expired, displaced) is a
`404` instead.

SignInLink.description:
The sign-in link from `GET /auth/link`: a sign-in approved before it was asked for, its
claim secret in the fragment.

SignInRequest.description:
What `POST /pair` answers the page that asked: the claim secret this page alone polls
with, the short code it shows for the operator to approve at the host, and the seconds
both live.

Spot.description:
The spotter's verdict on one gated tool call (docs/permissions.md), logged as a
[`Payload::Spot`] audit entry. The `stance` is the graded disposition the
independent rung returned; the `reason` is its one-line rationale, addressed to
the acting session (what it reads to self-correct or petition). `origin` records
whether the verdict was the spotter model's or the fail-closed fallback (the one
signal the stance alone erases — a deliberate `gate` and a failed spotter call
both surface as `Gate`).

axes.description:
Every probability the decision rung answered, when that rung produced the
verdict (docs/permissions.md). The stance and reason are a fold over these
under the thresholds of the day; recording the vector is what lets a live
session's verdicts join the calibration corpus and replay under a different
band without re-asking. `None` from the prose rung, from a fail-closed
verdict, and on entries written before this field existed.

call_id.description: The `tool_use` id of the call this verdict judged.

model.description:
Which model returned this verdict, as **the response named itself** — the
same string `RequestUsage` carries, not the configured id, so a slug that
routes to something else records what actually answered.

A session's spotter is fixed at boot, so this is constant within a log;
it is recorded per entry anyway because the corpus that reads these
spans sessions and models, and attributing a verdict by re-deriving the
boot config is a join that can be wrong. `None` for a fail-closed verdict
(no request happened, so nothing answered) and for entries written before
this field existed — in both cases the absence is the honest reading.

probed_prefix.description:
The command prefix this spotter call was also asked to judge for **promotion**, if a
prefix-promotion probe rode along (docs/permissions.md). The probe's
answer *is* the stance — `ClearAlways` is the safe-vote for this prefix, any other stance is
not-safe — so the ledger that decides promotion folds from these `Spot` entries: a
`probed_prefix = Some(p)` with `origin = Model` contributes a vote for `p`. `None` when no
probe rode (most calls), so old logs and unprobed calls fold to nothing.

Stall.description:
A trajectory that ended without finishing (docs/transport.md).

The loop returns to idle on both failure paths above, which leaves the
daemon's other signals — the idle phase, no gate, an empty inbox once a
triage has dismissed the notification — identical to a run that
finished its work. This topic is the difference a supervising client reads:
set when the loop gives up, cleared when a trajectory next starts, so it
names the *current* condition rather than a past one (the same clear-on-
recovery rule the transport diagnostics follow).

at.description:
Unix millis at which the loop gave up — absolute, like every other
instant on the control channel, so nothing has to re-emit a ticking
field (docs/control-api.md).

attempts.description:
How many attempts were spent, where the failure path counts them;
`null` where it does not.

detail.description: The upstream's own words for the failure that ended the trajectory.

message.description:
Leads with what happened and what recovers it — the same register the
retry topic's `message` uses.

StallReason.description: Why a trajectory stopped short of finishing (docs/transport.md).

oneOf.description: The stream-abort budget was spent: every attempt died before finalizing.
The request itself failed after the transport's own retries.

The upstream named a failure no retry can change — an exhausted plan, a
rejected request, a bad credential — so the loop stalled on the first
attempt rather than spend the schedule (docs/transport.md).

The triage could not reach its model — the schedule ran out, or the
upstream refused — so the loop holds the batch's results, unshown, until a
retry succeeds or the operator interrupts (docs/triage.md).

The triage model answered every fork and never usably: a harness defect,
logged as one. The loop holds the results the same way
(docs/triage.md).

Stance.description:
The spotter's graded disposition for one move (docs/permissions.md). It splits
the fast-path's binary `Gate` into `Clear` (auto-approve, no human), `Watch` (a
middle stance that resolves to the human gate alongside `Gate` until a
watch-window maps it to an intervention latency), and `Gate`. [`Stance::ClearAlways`]
is a *refinement of `Clear`* the prefix-promotion probe adds: it clears the move **and**
votes the probed prefix blanket-safe (docs/permissions.md). Folding the
promotion answer into the stance — rather than a separate flag — makes the contradictory
combinations (`watch`/`gate` + "always safe") unrepresentable.

oneOf.description: Reversible-and-in-scope (or irreversible-but-scope-sanctioned): auto-approve.

Like [`Stance::Clear`] (auto-approve the move) **and** the probe's prefix is safe for *every*
argument under this mission — the safe-vote that drives prefix promotion. Only meaningful when
a probe rode the call (`Spot::probed_prefix` is `Some`); the move-approval path treats it
identically to `Clear`.

Probably fine but uncertain, or a one-way move worth a beat of attention.
Resolves to the human gate until the watch-window lands.
Out of scope or unsanctioned-irreversible: stop and ask the human.

StartFailure.description:
Why preparation ended without a session, and the turns sent while it was starting,
handed back for a client to put in a composer.

at.description: When it failed, absolute Unix millis.

withdrawn.description: The turns queued while starting, in submission order.

StartingStage.description: Which part of preparation is running (docs/control-api.md).

oneOf.description: Establishing the session's environment: the user-wide `env_hook` (docs/env.md).

`boot::prepare` or `boot::resume`: the config, the provider lookup, the MCP
mounts, the preamble.

StartingView.description:
The `starting` topic: a session reserved on the host whose environment and MCP
servers are being prepared, or whose preparation failed. `null` once the session has
started, which is every value a running session publishes.

authorizing.description: The MCP server whose authorization preparation waits on; `null` when none.

cwd.description: The project root holding the session, which a resume names.

failure.description:
Why preparation ended without a session; `null` while it runs, and after an
archive stopped it.

resume.description: Reopening a dormant session rather than creating one.

since.description: When preparation began, absolute Unix millis.

StateTopics.description:
`GET /state` for a running session: `last_seq`, and one field per state topic, each
named by its topic and holding the value its `state` frame carries. A session still
starting answers only `last_seq` and the four topics it publishes (`verbs`, `queued`,
`starting`, `status`).

ask.description: `ask`: the question put to the operator.

cold.description: `cold`: the prompt cache is believed to have expired.

config_repair.description: `config_repair`: the config file a human has to fix.

current_operations.description: `current_operations`: what is in flight beside the loop.

gate.description: `gate`: the call held for a decision.

last_seq.description:
The highest committed `seq`, `null` on an empty log. Not a topic: the log's
cursor rather than control state, so no frame carries it.

newer_version.description: `newer_version`: a release newer than the host.

notifications.description: `notifications`: ambient notifications not yet shown by a triage.

processes.description: `processes`: every running tool-spawned process, structure only.

queued.description: `queued`: turns submitted and not yet taken, in submission order.

resolved_review_level.description:
`resolved_review_level`: the review position in force — the dial, except that
`supervisor` with no live supervisor reviews as `spotter_human`.

starting.description: `starting`: always `null` once a session has started.

status.description: `status`: where the session stands, as one view.

supervisor.description:
`supervisor`: the session that answers this one's gates under the `supervisor`
review position.

triage_upstream_failure.description: `triage_upstream_failure`: the same, for a separate triage client.

upstream_failure.description: `upstream_failure`: the last non-success upstream response, until a 2xx.

verbs.description: `verbs`: what each loop route would answer now.

StatusBody.description: An answer whose word is all it has to say: `{"status": <word>}`.

StatusView.description: One session's status, as every surface renders it.

StatusWord.description: The word a route answers `status` with when it has acted on a request.

oneOf.description: `POST /turns`: the turn is queued or delivered (`TurnAccepted`).
`PUT /approvals/:call_id`: the decision reached the held call.
`POST /approvals/:call_id/escalate`: the call stays held, and the operator is asked.
`POST /loop/interrupt`: the running tool was signalled.
`POST /loop/continue`: the loop will take another turn on the wire it has.
`POST /loop/compact`: the session's model is writing the summary.
`DELETE /processes/:id`: the process's group was signalled.
`POST /push/subscriptions`: the subscription is recorded.
`DELETE /push/subscriptions`: the subscription is not held.
`POST /pair/claim`: the sign-in waits for the operator's approval.

StreamDelta.description:
A live, pre-commit output fragment streamed to clients as the control stream's
`output` class (docs/control-api.md). **Ephemeral and transport-only**:
never appended to the log, never projected, and droppable for a slow consumer.
The authoritative text always lands as a committed
[`LogEntry`](crate::record::log::LogEntry) on `/events`, so the stream is a live convenience
with the durable log as its backstop — which is exactly why it can ride a lossy
`broadcast` where `/events` must tail the log.
Every model-stream variant carries the content-block `index` it belongs to, and
`ToolCallStart` additionally the `tool_use` id: a fragment is partial delivery *of a
specific item*, and a client that cannot tell which holds one slot per kind and loses the
first tool call's arriving input the moment a second opens. [`ToolOutput`](Self::ToolOutput)
and [`ProcessOutput`](Self::ProcessOutput) key on their own ids for the same reason
(docs/control-api.md).

oneOf.description: A fragment of assistant prose as the model streams it from the upstream SSE.

A fragment of extended-thinking text as the model streams it. A separate variant from
[`AssistantText`](Self::AssistantText) because it is *not* the assistant's answer — a client
must render it as thinking or not at all, never as prose.

The model began emitting a tool call, named before its arguments stream. Together with
[`ThinkingText`](Self::ThinkingText) these are the output kinds that make a turn visible at all:
without them only prose reaches the stream, so a turn spent thinking or emitting a large
tool input publishes nothing and reads as a hung harness (docs/transport.md).

A fragment of a tool call's JSON input, verbatim. The bytes are passed through rather than
summarized as a count: they are a partial slice of a JSON document, so a client must not
*parse* them as if complete — but showing what actually arrived claims no structure, and
`{"command":"cargo test` tells an operator far more than a byte count does. (Rendering a
partial document *structurally* is a real option — `jiter`'s partial mode, `actson`'s push
parser — and is filed as its own design question.)
A chunk of a running tool's combined output, tagged by its `tool_use` id.

A chunk of a running background process's output, tagged by the process's
spawn-minted id — rendered `p#<n>` in prose, bare here (docs/process-monitor.md).
Demuxed by id exactly like
[`ToolOutput`](Self::ToolOutput) is by `call_id`. Lossy: a cold-opened client
seeds its tail from the process resource and layers these on top.

A fragment of the summary a compaction is writing (docs/summary.md).
Not the main loop's response: it belongs to no content block of one, and the
committed `Assistant` entry that retires the block variants does not retire it.
The finished text lands as the compaction's `Summary`; these are lossy and never
logged.

A fragment of the compaction's extended thinking, the counterpart of
[`CompactionText`](Self::CompactionText).
Extended thinking from the same detached consolidation request.

A fragment of the text a triage request is writing (docs/triage.md), whichever
shape runs it. Not the main loop's response, so it carries no block `index` and a
committed `Assistant` entry does not retire it. `call_ids` are the `tool_use` ids
of the results being triaged; empty for the idle triage, which has none. Lossy and
never logged: the verdict lands as the `Triage` entries.

A fragment of the triage request's extended thinking, the counterpart of
[`TriageText`](Self::TriageText).

StreamDiagnostics.description:
What the transport saw on the response that produced an empty finalized
stream (docs/transport.md).

Every field is optional-ish on purpose: this is evidence, not a contract, and
a missing piece must not cost the pieces that are present. Values pass the
log's `[env]` masker like any other stored text (docs/env.md).

frames.description:
The stream re-rendered from its decoded events, one `event:` / `data:`
pair per frame in arrival order. Not the socket's bytes: the SSE decoder
hands over decoded events, so comments and line folding are already gone.

frames_truncated.description:
Whether [`FRAME_CAPTURE_CAP`] stopped the capture — `frames` then holds
the head of the stream and nothing after it.

headers.description:
Response headers, restricted to [`is_captured_header`]. A response header
can carry account-scoped values, so the log stores a named set rather than
whatever the edge attached (docs/env.md).

message_start.description:
The `message_start` event's `data` payload as received, when one arrived.
Kept whole rather than reduced to parsed fields: OpenRouter's Messages
skin carries a top-level `provider` in the `message` object naming the
serving leg (docs/transport.md), and keeping the body whole means any
other unmodeled field survives without a schema change.

status.description:
The HTTP status the stream arrived on — 200 on this path, recorded rather
than assumed.

Summary.description:
The content of a [`Payload::Summary`]: `text` replaces the inclusive range
`from..=upto` of the transcript for the readers its `audience` names. A head
summary starts at `from == 0`; a working-span summary starts later. The entry
itself projects to nothing; the text appears where the range ends
(docs/summary.md, docs/log-and-projection.md).

audience.description: Which projection the summary applies to (docs/summary.md).

made_by.description: Who made `text` (docs/summary.md). Absent from a summary the agent made.

oneOf.description:
Per-call tool telemetry (docs/tools.md) — how long one call took, how it
came out, and how big its result was, appended right after the
[`ToolResult`] it describes.

A separate entry rather than a field on [`ToolResult`], which is the
shape [`Spot`] already uses for per-call audit: the pairing is by
`call_id`, the payload is written by a different concern than the result,
and [`ToolResult`] is constructed at dozens of sites (many of them a
harness stand-in with no run to measure) that would each have to name a
telemetry value they do not have.

[`ToolResult`]: super::Payload::ToolResult
[`Spot`]: super::Payload::Spot

A call's dispatch is about to reach the world: appended after the permission
cascade clears it and before the tool runs. A call with this and no result may
have had side effects, which is the one state a resumed session can't continue
from.

One stage of one upstream request — sent, an attempt that failed, first byte,
ended, failed. Telemetry for "what was it doing, and since when" and the source
of the `current_operations` topic (docs/control-api.md); the entry's `at` is the
stage's time.

One step of a moment's push: decided, held, released, cancelled, or the push
services' answers (docs/web-push.md). The entry's `at` is the step's time.

One step of the cold check: the loop parked, a person released it, the park
ended (docs/control-api.md). The entry's `at` is the step's time.

A compaction was asked for and accepted (`POST /loop/compact`, docs/summary.md):
whether the operator gave up a warm cache for it, and the last seq the summary
will cover. Its summarizing request follows as `RequestStage` entries with the
`compaction` origin, then the compaction's `Summary` on success or a
[`CompactionFailed`](Self::CompactionFailed). The compaction's state on
`/state` is folded from these (docs/control-api.md).

The compaction asked for last did not land a summary: the error that ended it,
a superseding turn included (docs/summary.md).

A shown notification no triage verdict mentioned was dismissed by the harness
after `shows` triages displayed it (docs/inbox.md). The entry resolves the
notification the way a `Dismiss` would, and records that the model did not make
the choice.

The session's supervisor was set or cleared after creation
(docs/permissions.md): the session now named, or `None` when cleared. The
creator a session starts with is in the header and is not recorded here.

An interrupt reached the loop (`POST /loop/interrupt`, docs/control-api.md):
who sent it and through which affordance, appended before the signal fires so
it precedes the `failed: interrupted` stage it causes. Appended whether or not
anything was running.

A decision on a held call was accepted (`PUT /approvals/:call_id`, the
in-session approve; docs/control-api.md): which call, what was decided, and
who decided it. Appended once the call is known to be the pending gate and
before the decision reaches the loop, so it precedes the result or the
redirect it causes. A redirect the loop's own permission review writes is
recorded under `review[<level>]`; a spotter clear leaves none.

A held call was escalated: whoever it was routed to passed it up without deciding
it (`decide` with `escalate`, docs/permissions.md). It stays held, now routed to
`to`. Appended when the escalation is accepted, so it precedes the decision that
eventually resolves the call.
A main-model consolidation check and its disposition (docs/consolidate.md).

The `tools[]` the session advertises, as sent: appended at boot, and at a resume
when it differs from the last one recorded (docs/resumption.md). The array is
kept as `Value`s, whose object keys serialize sorted, so equal tool sets are
equal values. Offline readers (`dev wire`, the triage replay) rebuild the request
from it instead of from current code.

Timestamp.description:
Wall-clock millis since the Unix epoch. **Log metadata only**: timestamps are
never projected onto the wire, so their non-determinism cannot affect cache
stability (docs/log-and-projection.md).

Title.description: One title decision (docs/session-title.md): the text and who wrote it.

TitleAuthor.description:
Who set a [`Title`]: the triage model's title ask, or an operator over the control
channel (docs/session-title.md).

ToolCall.description:
A tool invocation emitted by the model. `input` is a [`serde_json::Value`],
whose object maps serialize with sorted keys — deterministic, sidestepping
the `HashMap`-key-order cache hazard (docs/log-and-projection.md).

ToolEntry.description:
One tool's full definition, addressed by wire name — the payload for
`GET /v1/tools/:name` (docs/control-api.md). A consumer fetches these
lazily, one at a time, rather than holding a table pushed at session
start: an MCP server may mount dozens of tools with long descriptions.

`description` and `annotations`/`title` are third-party prose for a
mounted server (`server.is_some()`): a consumer renders them as plain
text, never markdown, and attributes them to `server`
(`src/tools/process_monitor.rs` draws the same untrusted-server line for the
built-ins' own annotations).

input_schema.description:
Sent exactly as the model saw it this session, [`INTENT`] included
(docs/tools.md) — so a consumer comparing a call's arguments against
`required` sees the schema the call was actually made against, not a
pre-injection one that would flag `intent` as undeclared on every call.

name.description:
The wire name this entry was looked up by (`<server>__<tool>` or an
unprefixed embedded name) — echoed back so a caller that resolved a
dotted operator spelling can confirm what it landed on.

server.description:
The server that mounted this tool, or `None` for one of the harness's
own embedded tools (`bash`, `read_image`, the fs/semantic-edit MCP
servers) — the line [`ToolBrief::server`] already draws.

ToolOutcome.description:
How one tool call came out (docs/tools.md). Derived generically at the
dispatch point from `is_error`, which means *refusal* for built-in negative
outcomes — so the three classes are readable off every tool without per-tool
knowledge.

oneOf.description: The call did what it was asked to do.

The tool ran and declined: an anchor that matched nothing, a command that
exited non-zero, a path outside a grant. The model's next move is the
interesting one — this is the class whose recovery-on-next-attempt rate
says whether a cheap model spirals on the errors the `is_error` flip made
visible.

The harness could not run the call at all: no mounted tool owns the name,
or a background spawn failed. Distinct from [`Rejected`] because it is a
defect signal about the harness, not a datum about the model's judgment.

Set from an explicit flag at the sites that *construct* a harness-authored
failure, never inferred from result text. So an argument that would not
deserialize is **not** here: the tool returned that error itself, and a
model sending a string where the schema declares an array is a datum about
the model. It classifies as [`Rejected`].

[`Rejected`]: ToolOutcome::Rejected

ToolSettings.description:
One `[tools]` entry as written. A field left `None` comes from the namespace's entry, then
the default ([`Config::tool_enabled`], [`ToolsTable::granted`]). Serialized as the `role`
topic reports an entry, with only the fields it sets (docs/control-api.md).

ToolTelemetry.description:
What one tool call cost and how it came out (docs/tools.md), recorded per
call as a [`Telemetry::Tool`] entry.

It exists so that "did that edit apply or get refused" is a field rather than
a grep over result prose. Prose written for a model is not a measurement
surface — its wording is free to change for the model's sake, and a count
taken off it can measure a throttle rather than the thing it names.

Additive by construction: because it projects to nothing, growing this struct
cannot perturb the byte-stability pin (docs/log-and-projection.md) — the same
property every [`Telemetry`] entry has.

bash.description: Bash-specific fields, when the call was one.

call_id.description: The `tool_use` id — the join back to the call and its [`Payload::ToolResult`].

duration_ms.description:
Wall-clock milliseconds the dispatch took: the permission cascade is
*excluded* (a call that waited an hour at a human gate did not run for an
hour), and a backgrounded spawn is the spawn alone.

edit.description: Edit-shaped fields, when the call carried the arguments they read.

images.description:
Realized image blocks the result carried. Zero for every text tool;
defaulted and skipped so those entries stay small.

result_bytes.description:
Bytes of result text as the tool produced it — **before** the triage
triages it (docs/triage.md). The pair (this, the selection's
size) is what says how much a triage actually saved.

tool.description: The wire tool name, namespaced as the call carried it.

ToolsChange.description:
How a resumed session's `tools[]` differs from the last one recorded, by tool name.
Empty when the arrays are equal. `reordered` is set when the names and definitions are
the same and only their order moved, which is still a different request prefix.

changed.description: Same name, different definition (description or schema).

Triage.description:
A triage verdict (docs/triage.md) — what the model decided in a throwaway
triage, recorded durably so every triage decision is reconstructable from the log
(including ones only ever visible inside the fork). The rendered wire form lives
on the paired [`ToolResult`]'s [`WireState`]; this carries the *provenance* the
rendered output can't, with no overlap.

[`ToolResult`]: Payload::ToolResult

for_result.description:
The `seq` of the [`Payload::ToolResult`] this verdict triaged — `None` for a
**standalone** triage (the idle-triggered inbox-only triage, docs/inbox.md: a triage
that rides no tool result). Backward-compatible: serde reads an old bare `seq` as `Some`.

inbox.description:
Per-notification dispositions chosen in this triage, by the notification's
arrival `seq` (docs/inbox.md). Empty on a triage that was shown nothing.

origin.description:
Whether the verdict came from the model or a harness fallback. For a
model-free stub triager this is the one signal the rendered output
erases (its head/tail verdict renders like a deliberate one); a failed triage
additionally projects a withheld-output error (docs/triage.md).

raw_keep.description: The model's exact `keep` string, pre-parse (empty for a model-free triager).

retries.description:
One breadcrumb per **non-compliant triage attempt** this triage saw, in order,
attempt-stamped — recorded even when an in-fork retry recovered
(docs/triage.md). A runtime triage failure is a harness defect
signal, so it must survive to the log rather than only the daemon's stderr;
the compliance record is a fold over this field. Triage-scoped: rides the last
`Triage` of a batch, like `inbox`. `#[serde(default)]`: old logs read empty.

shown_through.description:
The last arrival this triage's rider showed (docs/inbox.md): every notification
whose arrival `seq` is at or below it, and with no verdict yet, was in front of
the model. Absent means this entry's own `seq`, which is what a log written before
the field recorded (a notification was logged when a triage first showed it, so it
sat just ahead of that triage). A triage that showed no rider records `Some(0)` (seq 0 is the boot `Preamble`),
and one that showed it records the highest `seq` the rider held, so a notification
that arrived while the request was in flight reads as new at the next triage.
[`project`] never reads it.

[`project`]: crate::record::project::project

surfaced.description:
Context items this triage chose to **surface** — names from the boot `Preamble`'s
structured listing (stub files with a `path`) the model judged relevant to the
work in flight (docs/triage.md). `project` re-renders each as a
read-me reminder at this entry's tail-ward position, off the listing (like a
pinned notification's body). Also the surfaced-once dedup source: a later triage's
roster excludes any name already here. `#[serde(default)]`: old logs read empty.

thinking.description:
The triage's own reasoning — the text of every thinking block the fork emitted,
one entry per attempt that produced any, in attempt order (docs/triage.md).
The fork runs under the same thinking policy as an agent turn (the shared
envelope), so most triages think; without this the log records *what* was decided
and never *why*. Signatures are not kept: this is a record, not a replay input —
the fork's transcript stays throwaway. Operator/developer observability only;
[`project`] never reads it, so recording it cannot move the wire.
`#[serde(default)]`: old logs read empty.

[`project`]: crate::record::project::project

TriageChoice.description:
The triage choice a session creator makes. Omission inherits the configured
default; `Shared` explicitly bypasses a configured separate default; `Separate`
carries the existing independent-client options.

connection.description:
Names the connection, making `model` a provider-native id. Absent, the
`model` string is the `connection/model` slug.

TriageIdentity.description:
Which client triages tool results: the main client (`shared`), or its own,
whose selection is then reported like the other roles. A shared triage reports
the main selection so two accounts on one model stay distinguishable.

TriageModel.description: Which inference the triage step ran on (docs/triage.md).

oneOf.description: Triage ran on the session's main inference.

Triage ran on its own inference, with the reasoning settings boot
resolved for it — the knob set that inference is called with, recorded
so a reader need not consult live configuration to reproduce the step.
A real `retain` call from the triage model.

The harness fallback — the triage failed (the result projects a withheld-output
error, docs/triage.md), or a model-free stub triager ran.

Triaged.description:
A triage verdict on one result (docs/triage.md): which lines survive,
the note read in their place, and triage's optional request for a better
`intent`. Carried by [`WireState::Triaged`]; the wire form is re-rendered from
`raw` plus this each turn, so a field added here is one setter and one render
clause, never a sweep.

intent_feedback.description:
Present only when the intent gave triage nothing to decide against — about
the intent and never the task (docs/triage.md). Rendered after the
note. Absent on logs written before the field existed, so it deserializes as
`None` and serializes only when set.

TurnAccepted.description:
The answer to `POST /turns`: the turn is enqueued, under the id it will be addressed by.
The id is informational: the turn's effects can arrive on the stream before this body
resolves.

submission_id.description: The id the client sent, or the one the host minted.

oneOf.description: A person acted and the request went out.
The belief ended without one (a compaction, or another request warmed the cache).

UpstreamFailure.description:
The latest upstream failure: optional HTTP status, consecutive occurrences,
and error detail. Cleared on HTTP 2xx; later stream failure sets it again.
Ephemeral transport diagnostics: never appended
to the log or projected (docs/transport.md).

anyOf.description: The failure with no diagnostics attached.
The failure with the evidence its stream captured.

UpstreamFailureRecord.description:
Why an assistant entry is record-only, plus the transport evidence when the
path that produced it captured any.

Serializes as a **bare string** when there are no diagnostics, which is the
shape every log before this type used, and deserializes from either shape —
so an old log line parses and an ordinary failure writes the same bytes it
always did.

UpstreamRetry.description:
A retry in flight: what a client renders while the loop is waiting out an
aborted stream (docs/transport.md).

`next_attempt_at` is an **absolute** instant rather than a countdown, so the
daemon never has to re-emit a ticking field — a client computes the remaining
wait itself (docs/control-api.md). It is control state, never projected, so the
wall-clock reading cannot reach the cached prefix.

attempt.description: Which attempt just failed — 1-based, so `attempt` of `budget` reads directly.

budget.description: Total attempts the loop will make before it gives up.

detail.description: The upstream's error text for the attempt that failed.

message.description:
Leads with what happened and what is being done about it — *stream aborted,
retrying (2 of 12)*. The status code and the upstream's own words are
`detail`, not the headline.

next_attempt_at.description: Unix millis at which the next attempt fires.

Usage.description:
The Anthropic `usage` object (docs/transport.md). `Default` seeds the
[`Assembler`] before `message_start` arrives.

Every field needs both `#[serde(default)]` and [`null_or_missing`], because
providers report a count they have nothing to say about in two different
ways: Anthropic omits the field, while OpenRouter-fronted upstreams send it
present with an explicit `null`. `default` alone covers only the absent case;
a present `null` still hits the `u64` and errors the whole response away.

UsageView.description:
The `usage` topic: token counts, the prompt cache's health, the session's cost, and
the Codex backend's plan windows, for the main loop and for a triage client of its own.

Every instant is absolute Unix millis, so the topic stays quiet until a request
happens: a client subtracts from its own clock (docs/control-api.md).

cold_streak.description:
Consecutive main-loop requests that read nothing from the cache and had no
legitimate reason to (docs/log-and-projection.md); 0 once a turn reads warm. A
number rather than a flag, so the threshold is the client's ([`COLD_STREAK_WARN`]).

context.description:
The boot-fetched context window and the last turn's prompt against it; `null`
when no capabilities were fetched.

cost.description:
The billed session total, where the provider has a per-request accounting
surface; `null` where it has none.

cumulative.description: The counts summed over every request the session has made.

keepalive_skipped.description:
The main keepalive's stance while it is not pinging on schedule; `null` while it
is, and when none is armed.

last.description: The last request's token counts, whatever it was for; `null` before the first.

last_cache_miss.description:
What the provider said about the most recent miss it attributed; `null` until one
arrives.

last_request_at.description:
The last request on the main prefix: a turn, a keepalive ping, or a triage on the
agent's own client. Persists across a host restart; `null` before the first.

plan.description:
The Codex backend's subscription windows as of the last response that named them;
`null` on every other provider.

retention.description:
How much of what the triage was shown survives on the wire (docs/triage.md),
folded from the log.

triage_cold_streak.description:
The same count over a separate triage client's reads; `null` while the triage
borrows the agent's client.

triage_keepalive_skipped.description: The triage lineage's keepalive stance, by the same rule.

triage_plan.description:
A separate triage client's own windows, in the same shape; `null` while the triage
borrows the agent's client, and when its provider reports none.

VerbAnswer.description:
One loop route's answer: `accepted`, and either what an accepted request would do or
the message a refusal carries.

delivery.description: An accepted turn's delivery: at once, or queued until the loop's next juncture.

message.description: A refusal's message: the one the route's `409` carries.

warm.description:
An accepted compaction's body: `true` where only a request saying `warm: true`
compacts, because the cache is believed live.

Verbs.description:
The `verbs` topic: what each loop route would answer now (docs/control-api.md), read
from the check the route itself runs. A client renders a refused verb disabled with
its message; a request that arrives after the topic moved is checked again.

turn.description:
`POST /turns`: always accepted while the session runs, with where the turn would
land.

WireState.description:
How a [`Payload::ToolResult`] should be projected. Flipping this (never
touching `raw`) is the one triage primitive — every projection experiment
is a change to how [`project`] reads these (docs/README.md, docs/log-and-projection.md).

Each variant is wired into [`project`] before it has a construction site, so a
new site lands as a behavior change rather than a type change that would move
the byte-stability pin. `Triaged` is built by the triage
(docs/triage.md); `Interrupted` by the interrupt (docs/control-channel.md). `Elided`
is no longer written; logs that carry it project as they did.

[`project`]: crate::record::project::project

oneOf.description:
Captured durably, but not yet accepted onto the main agent's wire.
An appended result verdict resolves this state (docs/triage.md).
Project the full `raw` content.

Project the **verdict** — which lines survive (`keep`) plus an optional `note`
— re-rendered from `raw` by [`project`] each turn, *not* the rendered bytes
(docs/triage.md). The kept bytes are never stored twice, and the
structured decision doubles as the record. `raw` stays in the log.

[`project`]: crate::record::project::project

Project nothing of substance; still recoverable from the log. Written by the
interrupt before it said who interrupted ([`WireState::Interrupted`]).

Project a fixed line saying the call was interrupted, by whom, and what became of
it; `raw` stays in the log (docs/control-channel.md). Recorded when the interrupt
lands, so the line is rendered from the log alone.

A result an earlier harness withheld as a hard error because its triage had no
verdict. **No longer written**: a triage without a verdict now holds its
results until it has one (docs/triage.md). Kept so logs that carry it
still load and project as they did — a hard error in place of the output
(`is_error` forced true), `raw` still in the log.

WithdrawnTurns.description:
The answer to `DELETE /turns/:submission_id`: the turns the recall popped, in the order they
were submitted. Empty when the loop had already taken them.

base.description:
The commit the checkout is on: the creator's `HEAD` for an add; the branch tip
or the project's `HEAD` for a restore.

exit_code.description:
Git's exit status; `None` when a signal ended it. Nonzero with an existing
directory is a failed `post-checkout` hook.

WorktreeEvent.description: One event in a session's own worktree.

oneOf.description: Created at session creation, on a new branch.
Re-created on resume, from the kept branch or a fresh one at the project's `HEAD`.
Removed on archive because it held no uncommitted work.

branch_deleted.description: Whether the branch was deleted too: only when another branch contains its tip.

oneOf.description: Left in place on archive.
Git failed to inspect or remove it on archive.
